inventory reports success while the thing it checks is broken.

catch false passes have false-passed many times, and the most recent instance was
in this round's own subject. The push guard's first self-test reported every

**Seam 2 — rename and pre-push guard**

GitHub’s quoted rename behaviour is accurate. Old Git URLs redirect after rename; reusing the old repository name ends that redirect. The sibling repositories’ visibility and creation dates also match D4. [GitHub rename documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/renaming-a-repository).

Local experiments with Git **2.50.1** established:

| Route | What happened / design consequence |
|---|---|
| `url.<base>.insteadOf` | Hook received the **rewritten destination**, not the original alias |
| `remote.origin.pushurl` | Hook received the **push URL** |
| `--no-verify` | Push succeeded without invoking the hook |
| `core.hooksPath` override | Push succeeded without invoking the installed hook |
| Fresh clone | Repository-local hook was absent; push succeeded |
| Linked second worktree | Shared the hook and was refused; a second worktree is **not automatically a bypass** |
| `gh repo create --source . --push` | CLI source delegates to Git push; it does **not inherently bypass** an effective hook |
| Remote `gh repo sync` | Uses GitHub APIs, so no local hook runs; this does not establish that unrelated private objects would be accepted |
| IDE | A normal Git invocation normally runs the hook; an alternative Git implementation or overridden configuration needs separate verification |

Sources: [Git hooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks), [CLI create implementation](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/repo/create/create.go), [CLI sync implementation](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/repo/sync/sync.go).

The decisive experiment was a push from an unhooked toy clone into a repository with an unrelated public root:

```text
mixed_push_exit 1
main_rejected True
private_branch_published True
```

**`git push --all` rejected `main` but successfully created another branch containing the toy private history.** Main-branch protection and a failed push exit code therefore do not establish confidentiality.

- **R1-3 | HIGH | A repository-local URL hook does not close the private-history publication route | D:181–188,267–270; bypass and mixed-result push experiments above | Remove public-repository write authority from private-history environments; reserve publication credentials for the isolated export. Keep the hook as an additional guard, preferably allowing only the canonical private destination.**

A URL expression must account for owner/repository case, optional `.git`, trailing slash, scp-style SSH and `ssh://` forms. It should inspect Git’s effective destination, not reconstruct it from `origin`. A blacklist remains weaker than a private-destination allowlist.

One qualification to the proposed test: after the rename, the old URL can still resolve to the renamed private repository. Thus testing before public creation can invoke the hook. Require its **specific refusal marker**; an authentication or repository-not-found error is not proof that it ran.

| Measurement | Result |

The titles concern subjects already described in the public tracked material; I found no title-specific leak.

Issues, PRs and Discussions must all be kept out of the initial numbering sequence. Transfers and integrations that create them also matter. A push, workflow run, label or release does not itself reserve an issue number. This workflow has read-only permissions and no creation step. Enabling Discussions can lead through creation of a welcome discussion, so defer that setup too. [GitHub Discussions setup](https://docs.github.com/en/discussions/quickstart).

Creating the repository privately is useful, but **privacy alone does not reserve numbers**. Assert each returned number as it is created, and stop immediately on a mismatch.

The semantic question remains **uncleared**. The allowed queries establish that #5 and #8 have no `U-nn` references and #10 has one U-32-bearing paragraph. They cannot establish that other paragraphs paraphrase no withheld observation. I did not evade the transcript restriction to read those bodies.

- **R1-4 | MEDIUM | The publishable issue payloads and semantic-redaction gate are not concretely bound | D:234,271–275; open issues have three comments between them, while step 9 scans “13 bodies” | Specify title plus sanitized body only, explicitly exclude comments/attachments, complete the semantic review, and create each issue from the exact swept file. Freeze those files rather than re-fetching bodies during creation.**
- **R1-5 | MEDIUM | The universal stub promise is false | D:238–240; REVIEW-013 request:15,161 still presents the unresolved re-weigh, whose final disposition is in `docs/reviews/REVIEW-013c-adjudication-option-2-and-amendments-2026-08-18.md:10` | Give each closed stub a verified outcome-document link; remove the promise that every citing document contains the outcome.**

Step 9 does not explicitly authorize copying comments, but “full copies” invites that interpretation. If comments are copied, the specified body-only sweep has not covered the complete publication payload.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# wconf push guard — the pre-push hook for this repository's PRIVATE clones.
#
# Decision request phase 1, D4. Installed by `make install-push-guard`, which
# copies this file into the clone's hooks directory and records two values in
# the clone's git config: the private archive's GitHub repository id, and the
# root commits of the private history.
#
# The property: a push that carries the private history goes to the private
# archive and nowhere else. "Carries" means a pushed commit has a recorded root
# as an ancestor. "The archive" means the destination's GitHub repository id
# equals the recorded one and GitHub reports it private. The id survives a
# rename, so the check holds before the rename, after it, and while the new
# public repository is still private, which a visibility check alone would not.
#
# Measured on git 2.50.1 before this was written: git passes the destination
# AFTER `insteadOf`, `pushInsteadOf` and `pushurl` are applied, and runs the
# hook once for every push URL of a remote.
#
# ⚠ A guard against mistakes, not against the owner. `git push --no-verify`
# skips it, and it does nothing in a clone it was never installed in.
#
# `make check-push-guard` breaks it every way it knows and fails if any break
# goes unnoticed.
set -u

# Prints `owner/name` for a GitHub URL, or fails. Hosts are matched exactly, so
# `github.com.example.org` is not GitHub.
parse_github_url() {
  local u=$1 rest hostpart host path
  case "$u" in
    https://* | http://* | ssh://* | git://*)
      rest=${u#*://}
      hostpart=${rest%%/*}
      [ "$hostpart" = "$rest" ] && return 1
      path=${rest#*/}
      ;;
    *:*)
      # scp-like `[user@]host:path`, which git takes only when no `/` comes
      # before the first `:`.
      hostpart=${u%%:*}
      case "$hostpart" in */*) return 1 ;; esac
      path=${u#*:}
      ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  hostpart=${hostpart##*@}
  host=$(printf '%s' "${hostpart%%:*}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  case "$host" in
    github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
  path=${path%.git}
  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
  case "$path" in
    */*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;
    ?*/?*) ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$path"
}

if [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && [ "$1" = "--parse-url" ]; then
  parse_github_url "$2"
  exit
fi

url=${2-}
refuse() {
  printf 'push guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2
  printf '  destination: %s\n' "$url" >&2
  printf '  This history may go only to the private archive. Publish from the\n' >&2
  printf '  export instead: decision request phase 1, item 5, step 4.\n' >&2
  exit 1
}

roots=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.roots || true)
archive_id=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid || true)
if [ -z "$roots" ] || [ -z "$archive_id" ]; then
  refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"
fi
for r in $roots; do
  git cat-file -e "${r}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
    || refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"
done

carries=0
# `|| [ -n … ]` keeps a last line with no newline. git always sends one; the
# guard should not depend on it.
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do
  [ -n "${local_sha-}" ] || continue
  # A deletion publishes nothing.
  case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
  if ! commit=$(git rev-parse -q --verify "${local_sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null); then
    carries=1
    break
  fi
  for r in $roots; do
    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$r" "$commit" 2>/dev/null
    case $? in
      0) carries=1; break 2 ;;
      1) ;;
      *) carries=1; break 2 ;;
    esac
  done
done
[ "$carries" = 0 ] && exit 0

target=$(parse_github_url "$url") \
  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and the destination is not a GitHub repository"
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and gh is not on PATH, so the destination cannot be checked"
info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private)"' 2>/dev/null) \
  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"
id=${info%% *}
private=${info#* }
[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ] \
  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and $target (repository id $id) is not the archive (id $archive_id)"
[ "$private" = "true" ] \
  || refuse "$target is the archive, but GitHub reports that it is not private"
exit 0
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push, in this clone.
#
# Run it in every PRIVATE clone (decision request phase 1, D4 and item 5,
# step 8). It records the archive as the GitHub repository behind the clone's
# own push URL — so run it while `origin` is the private archive, under either
# name — and refuses if GitHub does not report that repository private.
#
# The hook is COPIED, not linked. A link into the tracked file would vanish on
# checking out any commit that predates it, and git treats a missing hook as
# no hook.
#
# Usage: tools/install-push-guard.sh [remote]   (default: origin)
set -euo pipefail

fail() { printf 'install-push-guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
src="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
[ -f "$src" ] || fail "$src is missing"

if hooks_path=$(git config --get core.hooksPath); then
  fail "core.hooksPath is set ($hooks_path), so a hook copied into the hooks directory would not run"
fi
hooks_dir=$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)
case "$hooks_dir" in /*) ;; *) hooks_dir="$top/$hooks_dir" ;; esac
dest="$hooks_dir/pre-push"
if [ -e "$dest" ] && ! grep -q '^# wconf push guard' "$dest"; then
  fail "$dest exists and is not this guard; move it aside first"
fi

remote=${1:-origin}
push_url=$(git remote get-url --push "$remote") || fail "no remote named $remote"
target=$(bash "$src" --parse-url "$push_url") \
  || fail "$remote's push URL is not a GitHub repository: $push_url"
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "gh is not on PATH"
info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private) \(.full_name)"') \
  || fail "could not read repos/$target from GitHub"
read -r archive_id private full_name <<<"$info"
[ "$private" = "true" ] || fail "$full_name is not private, so it cannot be the archive"

roots=$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
roots=${roots% }
[ -n "$roots" ] || fail "this clone has no commits"

git config wconf.pushguard.archiveid "$archive_id"
git config wconf.pushguard.archivename "$full_name"
git config wconf.pushguard.roots "$roots"
mkdir -p "$hooks_dir"
cp "$src" "$dest"
chmod 0755 "$dest"

printf 'push guard installed: %s\n' "$dest"
printf '  archive: %s (repository id %s, private)\n' "$full_name" "$archive_id"
printf '  roots:   %s\n' "$roots"
printf '  A push carrying a commit with one of those roots may go only to that\n'
printf '  repository id. It does not run on git push --no-verify, in a clone it\n'
printf '  was never installed in, or if core.hooksPath is set later.\n'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-test for the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push.
#
# Every case runs against the real hook, installed by the real installer into a
# throwaway repository, with a fake `gh` on PATH so nothing touches GitHub.
# Then every case runs again against MUTANTS of the hook, each of which removes
# one protection. A mutant that the cases do not catch fails this check, and so
# does a mutation that does not apply: a case list that a broken hook still
# passes proves nothing.
#
# Needs bash, git and perl. No network.
set -u

top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
HOOK_SRC="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
INSTALL_SRC="$top/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/push-guard.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

G() {
  git -c user.name=guard -c user.email=guard@example.invalid \
      -c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false -c init.defaultBranch=main "$@"
}
ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
FAILED=0
fail() { printf '  ✗ %s\n' "$1"; FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); }
pass() { printf '  ✓ %s\n' "$1"; }

if hp=$(git config --global --get core.hooksPath); then
  printf 'check-push-guard: FAIL — core.hooksPath is set globally (%s), so the guard cannot run on this machine\n' "$hp"
  exit 1
fi

# --- a fake gh, answering `gh api repos/<owner>/<name> --jq <expr>` from a table
mkdir -p "$work/bin" "$work/minbin"
cat >"$work/bin/gh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
[ "${1-}" = api ] || exit 2
want=$(printf '%s' "${2#repos/}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
while read -r name id private; do
  if [ "$(printf '%s' "$name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" = "$want" ]; then
    case "${4-}" in
      *full_name*) printf '%s %s %s\n' "$id" "$private" "$name" ;;
      *) printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$private" ;;
    esac
    exit 0
  fi
done <"$FAKE_GH_TABLE"
echo 'HTTP 404: Not Found' >&2
exit 1
EOF
chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
for t in bash git tr; do ln -s "$(command -v "$t")" "$work/minbin/$t"; done
PATH_GH="$work/bin:$PATH"
PATH_NO_GH="$work/minbin"

TABLE="$work/table"
printf 'arch/ive 100 true\npub/lic 200 true\nflip/ped 300 false\n' >"$TABLE"
TABLE_FLIPPED="$work/table-flipped"
printf 'arch/ive 100 false\npub/lic 200 true\n' >"$TABLE_FLIPPED"

# --- the "private" clone: a history with one root, then the guard installed
P="$work/private"
G init -q "$P"
G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m second
ROOT=$(G -C "$P" rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)
PRIV=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)
mkdir -p "$P/tools/git-hooks"
cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$P/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
G -C "$P" remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git

echo "The installer:"
if out=$(cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1); then
  pass "installs against a private archive"
else
  fail "installs against a private archive: $out"
fi
[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid)" = 100 ] \
  && pass "records the archive's repository id" || fail "records the archive's repository id"
[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.roots)" = "$ROOT" ] \
  && pass "records the history's root" || fail "records the history's root"
cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push" \
  && pass "copies the hook byte for byte" || fail "copies the hook byte for byte"

installer_refuses() { # <label> <needle> <setup...>
  local label=$1 needle=$2 d="$work/inst.$RANDOM"
  shift 2
  G init -q "$d" && G -C "$d" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
  mkdir -p "$d/tools/git-hooks"
  cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$d/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
  cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$d/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
  (cd "$d" && "$@")
  local o rc
  o=$(cd "$d" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "$o" | grep -qF "$needle"; then pass "$label"; else fail "$label (exit $rc): $o"; fi
}
installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not private" "is not private" \
  git remote add origin https://github.com/flip/ped.git
installer_refuses "refuses when core.hooksPath is set" "core.hooksPath is set" \
  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && git config core.hooksPath .hooks'
installer_refuses "refuses to overwrite a foreign pre-push hook" "is not this guard" \
  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && printf "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n" > .git/hooks/pre-push'
installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not on GitHub" "not a GitHub repository" \
  git remote add origin "$work/somewhere.git"

# History created AFTER the install, as it would be in the real clone.
G -C "$P" tag -a -m t ptag "$PRIV"
TAGOBJ=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse ptag)
G -C "$P" checkout -q --orphan clean
G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m orphan

G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.archiveid 100
G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.roots 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111

ref() { printf 'refs/heads/main %s refs/heads/main %s\n' "$1" "$ZERO"; }

# One case: <name> <0|1> <needle or -> <url> <stdin> [repo] [PATH] [table]
case_result() {
  local name=$1 want=$2 needle=$3 url=$4 input=$5 repo=${6:-$P} path=${7:-$PATH_GH} table=${8:-$TABLE}
  local out rc
  out=$(cd "$repo" && printf '%s' "$input" | PATH="$path" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$table" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push" origin "$url" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  if [ "$want" = 0 ]; then
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]
  else
    [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && { [ "$needle" = - ] || printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF "$needle"; }
  fi
}

NOT_ARCHIVE="is not the archive"
NOT_GITHUB="is not a GitHub repository"
CASES=(

  "R8|1|$NOT_GITHUB|file://$work/public.git|PRIV"
  "R9|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com.example.org/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
  "R10|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://example.org/github.com/arch/ive|PRIV"
  "R11|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://gitlab.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
  "R12|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com/arch/ive/extra|PRIV"
  "R13|1|could not be read|https://github.com/no/such|PRIV"
  "R14|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|TAG"
  "R15|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|MIXED"
  "R16|1|gh is not on PATH|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|NOGH"
  "R17|1|is not private|https://github.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV|FLIPPED"
  "R18|1|not configured|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|UNCONF"
  "R19|1|is not in this clone|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|SHALLOW"
  "O1|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|ORPH"
  "O2|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|DELETE"
  "O3|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|EMPTY"
)
CASE_COUNT=${#CASES[@]}

# Runs every case; prints the names that fail, one per line.
run_cases() {
  local c name want needle url what mode input repo path table
  for c in "${CASES[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r name want needle url what mode <<<"$c"
    repo=$P path=$PATH_GH table=$TABLE
    case "$what" in
      PRIV) input=$(ref "$PRIV") ;;
      TAG) input=$(printf 'refs/tags/ptag %s refs/tags/ptag %s\n' "$TAGOBJ" "$ZERO") ;;
      MIXED) input=$(ref "$ORPH"; printf 'refs/heads/two %s refs/heads/two %s\n' "$PRIV" "$ZERO") ;;
      ORPH) input=$(ref "$ORPH") ;;
      DELETE) input=$(printf '(delete) %s refs/heads/old %s\n' "$ZERO" "$PRIV") ;;
      EMPTY) input= ;;
    esac
    case "${mode-}" in
      NOGH) path=$PATH_NO_GH ;;
      FLIPPED) table=$TABLE_FLIPPED ;;
      UNCONF) repo=$U ;;
      SHALLOW) repo=$S ;;
    esac
    case_result "$name" "$want" "$needle" "$url" "$input" "$repo" "$path" "$table" || echo "$name"
  done
}

echo
echo "The hook, ${CASE_COUNT} cases:"
failed_cases=$(run_cases)
if [ -z "$failed_cases" ]; then
  pass "all ${CASE_COUNT} cases"
else
  for n in $failed_cases; do fail "case $n"; done
fi

echo
echo "Through git itself:"
G init -q --bare "$work/public.git"
if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
  fail "a real push of the private history is refused"
else
  G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/main >/dev/null \
    && fail "a real push of the private history is refused (but the ref arrived)" \
    || pass "a real push of the private history is refused, and nothing arrives"
fi
if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" clean 2>/dev/null) \
   && [ "$(G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse refs/heads/clean)" = "$ORPH" ]; then
  pass "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
else
  fail "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
fi
if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q --dry-run "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
  fail "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
else
  pass "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
fi

# --- mutants: each removes one protection, and the named case must catch it
echo
echo "Mutants — each must be caught by the case named:"
# Four parallel arrays, because several patterns contain `|`.
M_MUST=() M_LABEL=() M_FROM=() M_TO=()
mutant() { M_MUST+=("$1"); M_LABEL+=("$2"); M_FROM+=("$3"); M_TO+=("$4"); }
mutant R1 "ancestry not detected" '0) carries=1; break 2 ;;' '0) ;;'
mutant R1 "every ref skipped" 'case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac' 'continue'
mutant R1 "repository id not compared" '[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ]' 'true'
mutant R9 "host matched loosely" 'github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;' '*github.com*) ;;'
mutant R12 "extra path segments accepted" "*/*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;" "/* | */ | '') return 1 ;;"
mutant R13 "fail-open when GitHub cannot be read" '|| refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"' '|| exit 0'
mutant R15 "only the first pushed ref read" 'while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' 'read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; for _once in 1; do'
mutant R1 "a last line with no newline dropped" ' || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' '; do'
mutant R17 "archive's visibility not checked" '[ "$private" = "true" ]' 'true'
mutant R18 "unconfigured clone allowed" 'refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"' 'exit 0'
mutant R19 "absent root not refused" '|| refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"' '|| true'
MUTANT_COUNT=${#M_MUST[@]}
# A mutant counts as caught only if its case passed on the real hook. If the real
# hook fails any case, every mutant would look caught, so none is evaluated.
if [ -n "$failed_cases" ]; then
  fail "no mutant evaluated: the real hook fails cases, so a mutant's failures would prove nothing"
  M_MUST=()
fi
for i in "${!M_MUST[@]}"; do
  must=${M_MUST[$i]} label=${M_LABEL[$i]}
  for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do
    cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
    FROM=${M_FROM[$i]} TO=${M_TO[$i]} perl -0pi -e 's/\Q$ENV{FROM}\E/$ENV{TO}/' "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
  done
  if cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push"; then
    fail "mutant '$label' did not apply — the pattern no longer matches the hook"
    continue
  fi
  caught=$(run_cases)
  if printf '%s\n' "$caught" | grep -qx "$must"; then
    pass "'$label' is caught by $must"
  else
    fail "'$label' is NOT caught by $must (cases failing: $(printf '%s' "$caught" | tr '\n' ' '))"
  fi
done
for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"; done

echo
echo "What this does not check:"
echo "  1. git push --no-verify, which skips every hook; a clone the guard was never"
echo "     installed in; and core.hooksPath set after the install."
echo "  2. Real GitHub. gh is faked here. make install-push-guard reads the real"
echo "     archive, and a git push --dry-run to a real public repository proves the"
echo "     refusal without sending anything."
echo "  3. The hook treats a merge-base error as carrying the private history. No case"
echo "     produces that error, so that branch has no mutant."
echo
if [ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=PASS cases=%d mutants=%d exit=0\n' "$CASE_COUNT" "$MUTANT_COUNT"
  exit 0
fi
printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=FAIL failures=%d exit=1\n' "$FAILED"
exit 1

to you with a recommendation.

**Ruled A, and DONE 2026-10-18 (`REVIEW-056e`).** Round three found 9 findings, no

### D2. The revision log in a squashed repository

**Context, measured.** `docs/CLAIMS-REVISIONS.md` is derived from git history, and
`make check-claims-revisions` fails it if a commit it names is not an ancestor.
In the rehearsal repository it failed: *"db2fd12 is not an ancestor of HEAD"*.

| option | cost | what it buys |

Rehearsed, and `make ci` then passed every step in the export | the per-row dating survives as a record, and the gate keeps protecting the register going forward |

### D3. The licence, and the vendored `mpt-crypto` patch

**Context, searched on 2026-10-18 and re-measured that evening.** This repository is
Apache-2.0. It publishes `tools/spike-2026-08-18/wconf-nonces.patch`, 1,657 lines
against `XRPLF/mpt-crypto` at `85dbac7`, across six files under `src/`.

⚠ **This said *"with 341 context lines of upstream source"*, and that undercounted
it.** Counted by hunk, the patch has 756 added, 500 removed and 341 context lines,
and removed and context lines are both upstream source: **841 upstream lines, 764 of
them non-blank.** ⚠ An earlier revision of this paragraph said *"about 832"*, from a
pattern that skipped blank lines and lines starting `--`; `REVIEW-057` R1-2
re-counted it. ⚠ **A second file was not priced at all.**
`tools/mpt-crypto-bench/wconf_bench.c` says its setup code is *"lifted from the
corresponding upstream test"*. Of its 321 lines that are not blank, a comment or a
lone brace, 96 match a line of upstream's `tests/` at the pin exactly, and 101 after
trimming indentation. Some are API boilerplate.

⚠ **The records quote third-party source too, and this section first missed it**
(`REVIEW-057` R1-1, confirmed). `REVIEW-027`'s request packet reproduces the whole
of `ed25519-dalek` 2.2.0's `src/hazmat.rs`, and `REVIEW-024`'s quotes 139 lines of
the same crate, which is BSD-3-Clause: its copyright notice and conditions must
travel with the source. Packets also quote rippled, which is ISC, and XLS-0096,
whose repository is MIT, and both require their notice in copies. Under D5 the
records keep their wording, so the `NOTICE` has to cover them, and any quoted
`mpt-crypto` source in them stands where the patch does. 133 records mention
*verbatim* or a primary source, so the `NOTICE` waited for a scripted inventory of
every quoted third-party file with its project and licence. That inventory was step
1, and it is done; see below.

**That C repository carries no licence that these searches found:** `gh api repos/XRPLF/mpt-crypto/license`
returns 404, the root listing has no licence file at the pin or at `main`,
`conanfile.py` declares none, and no file under `src/` or `include/` has an SPDX
line, a licence text or a copyright line. No issue or pull request in it mentions
a licence; a control query in the same search returned hits, so the empty result
is real.

⚠ **The npm package's ISC licence is not evidence about the C source.**
`@xrplf/mpt-crypto@0.1.0` names `XRPLF/xrpl.js` as its repository, and ships
TypeScript and a WASM build of `mpt-crypto` 1.0.4 with no C source. Its `LICENSE`
is an ISC notice with the line *"Copyright (c) 2015 Ripple Labs Inc."*. Option A as
first written cited it as covering the C code, which is a substituted source.

⚠ **Nothing in the tree carves the upstream lines out of Apache-2.0.** `LICENSE`
is the only licence file and there is no `NOTICE`, so the publication as built
would appear to license Ripple's code under Apache-2.0.

| option | cost | what it buys |
|---|---|---|
| **A′. Publish the patch and the harness, with a `NOTICE` that carves them out** *(recommended; ruled)* | an inventory of quoted third-party source, one `NOTICE` file and one README line, committed before the export | a stranger can rebuild the signer, and the tree stops appearing to relicense upstream code. ⚠ The redistribution itself stays unlicensed, and is accepted by name |
| A. Publish the patch, citing the npm package's ISC licence | none now | ⚠ **not recommended**: it rests on a grant nothing states |
| B. Ask upstream to add a licence file first, then A | an upstream filing and its wait | **ruled out by the owner, 2026-10-18** |
| C. Publish without the patch or the lifted harness | the signer becomes buildable only from the private archive | no upstream code is republished; **the fallback if the copyright holder objects** |
| D. Move the patch to a GitHub fork of `mpt-crypto` | rework `tools/rebuild-env.sh` and `make vendor-verify`, and rebuild the signer, just before publication | the copy rests on GitHub's forking grant. ⚠ It does not settle modification: *"Although a code host such as GitHub may allow you to view and fork the code, this does not imply that you are permitted to use, modify, or share the software"* (choosealicense.com, read 2026-10-18) |

**Why A′ over C.** The signer is the main thing this project built, and its point
is that a claim is checked by running it. Under C a stranger cannot build it. The
practical risk under A′ is low: the code is published openly by the organisation
whose surrounding stack is ISC, and this project's use of it sends findings back
upstream. A′ cannot make the copy licensed. What it does is stop this repository
from mislabelling someone else's code, which is the part of the risk this project
controls.

**The `NOTICE` is written, in step 1, from a measured inventory** rather than a
draft. `tools/inventory-third-party.ts` compared every tracked file against 108
corpora in 91 projects: `mpt-crypto`, rippled, clio, XRPL-Standards and the dev
portal at stated versions, every crate the signer locks and every direct npm
dependency. **Six projects are reproduced**: `mpt-crypto`, which has no licence;
`ed25519-dalek`, BSD-3-Clause; rippled and `ripple-binary-codec`, ISC; and
XRPL-Standards and the dev portal, MIT. Each one's licence file is copied verbatim
into `LICENSES/`, and `make inventory-third-party` fails if `NOTICE` omits a project
the inventory finds, which was proved by removing one. The full list, with line
ranges and the method's blind spots, is `docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md`.

Plan item 6, attribution, also asks that every third-party citation name its
upstream and that P-7's credits be right on every public surface. **That check
was not run this session**, beyond the README's credit section, which now names
all three audits.

### D4. The public repository's name and owner

**Recommended and ruled: the public repository is `nandanito/xrpl-confidential-positions`,
and the private one is renamed `xrpl-confidential-positions-private` first.** That
is the pattern the EVM study already uses. `nandanito/evm-confidential-positions-private`
is private and `nandanito/evm-confidential-positions` is public, created the next
day (both read with `gh repo view` on 2026-10-18). The private repository holds the
name today, so the name has to be freed before the public one can take it. The
personal account matches the blog and the LinkedIn post. An organisation adds
nothing for a single-maintainer research artifact.

**The rename, read on GitHub's rename page on 2026-10-18.** After a rename, *"all
existing information, with the exception of project site URLs, is automatically
redirected to the new name."* If a new repository then takes the old name,
*"redirects to the renamed repository will no longer work."* Here that is what is
wanted: the canonical name should land on the public repository. Every existing
clone needs `git remote set-url origin` to the new name. The page also says
*"GitHub will not redirect calls to an action hosted by a renamed repository"*;
this repository hosts no action.

**Ruled, with one addition: the local folder keeps its name.** This checkout stays
at `…/xrpl-confidential-positions`. Claude Code's memory is keyed by the folder's
path, and the owner found that renaming the EVM study's folder broke both its Claude
Code and its Codex sessions. Only its `origin` changes, to `xrpl-confidential-positions-private`. The
public repository's working copy is a separate folder, the step 4 export.

⚠ **That leaves a folder whose name matches the PUBLIC repository holding the
PRIVATE history**, and one mistake publishes all of it: the history that
`--strict-history` fails on 1,045 personal-path hits, and the 36 commits behind the
withheld rows. Once the public repository takes the old name, a stale `origin` in
any clone stops redirecting to the archive and points at the public repository
instead. **So every private clone gets the push guard** (`make install-push-guard`),
and the public URL is never added as a remote here. ⚠ This first said the guard
would refuse URLs *"naming `nandanito/xrpl-confidential-positions` without the
`-private` suffix"*. It was built as an allowlist by repository id instead, and
what it does and does not close is D8.

The README's footnote records `xrpl-confidential-positions` as held since
2026-08-16, which stays true. The five-minute path says *"from a fresh clone"* and
names no URL, so nothing else changes.

### D7. Copying the issues, so the numbers the documents cite resolve

**Context, measured on 2026-10-18.** The README says bare issue numbers are issues
on *this* repository. `git grep` finds the pattern `issue #N` in 119 files, most of

These numbers belong to the private repository, which has 13 issues, three of them open (#5, #8, #10), 17
comments between them and no pull requests. A fresh public repository numbers from

at the wrong issue or at nothing.

⚠ **Six of the 13 cite withheld rows, and some restate them.** The bodies of #6
(U-28), #7 (U-31) and #10 (U-32), and comments on #2 (U-36), #3 (U-37) and #4
(U-35, U-38), cite rows that are in `docs/upstream-observed-WITHHELD.md` and not
in `UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md`. #10's body also restates what U-32 says. **Copying them
verbatim would publish part of what E-240 withheld.**

| option | cost | what it buys |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Title-only stubs for the ten closed issues, and full copies of the three open ones** *(recommended; ruled)* | 13 issues created in order, with #10's U-32 passage redacted and every body run through the secret sweep first | every cited number resolves, and no withheld row id leaves, because #10 is the only one of the open three that cites one. ⚠ The scan matched row ids, so the three open bodies still need a read for restated content. The closed issues' outcomes are already in the published register and reviews |
| B. Full copies of all 13 with their comments, after a redaction pass you approve | six issues redacted by hand and 17 comments copied | the discussions themselves become public |
| C. No copies. The step 6 sentence also says issue numbers refer to the archive, and the open three are re-filed under new numbers | the citations to #8 and #10 edited | ⚠ the public repository's own #1 to #13 would then collide with every cited number |

**What is published, exactly** (`REVIEW-057` R1-4). A copy is the title and a
body, and nothing else: no comments, attachments or labels. Each body is written to
a file, the owner reads the three open ones for any restatement of a withheld row
(the id scan cannot see a paraphrase), the files are swept, and each issue is
created from its own swept file with `gh issue create --body-file`. Nothing is
re-fetched from the archive at creation time.

A stub carries the original title and says: *"A stub. This was issue #N in the
private archive, opened DATE and closed DATE. Its discussion stays there."* ⚠ **It
said here that *"the outcome is in the document that cites it"*, and that is not
true of every citation** (R1-5): `REVIEW-013`'s request cites the re-weigh while it
was still open, and its outcome is in `REVIEW-013c`. So a stub links its outcome
only where a document is verified to record it, and otherwise says nothing about
one.

⚠ **The issues have to be created before anything else can take a number.** The
public repository is created private and made public only after them, Discussions
stay off until then, and each number GitHub returns is checked as it is created,
stopping at the first mismatch. Being private does not reserve a number by itself.

### D8. What keeps the private history out of the public repository

**Context.** `REVIEW-057` R1-3, upheld in part. A `pre-push` hook is not a
boundary: the leg measured that `--no-verify`, a fresh clone and `core.hooksPath`
each skip it. The plan, as frozen, described the hook as if it closed the route.
Since then the guard has been built as an allowlist rather than a URL pattern: a
push that carries the private history may go only to the archive, identified by
its GitHub repository id (`tools/git-hooks/pre-push`, `make check-push-guard`, in
`make ci`). It is installed in this clone and proved with dry runs. ⚠ **It stops
mistakes in a clone it is installed in, and nothing else.**

| option | cost | what it buys |
|---|---|---|
| **A. The guard, plus an inventory of every private clone** *(recommended)* | step 8 lists every clone on every machine, including any cloud session's checkout, and sets each one's `origin` and installs the guard | closes the realistic route, a stale `origin` after the public repository takes the old name. ⚠ **Residual, named**: a clone the inventory missed, or `--no-verify` |
| B. /bin/zsh -lc 'cat tools/inventory-third-party.ts docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md NOTICE LICENSES/*' in $USER_TMP/T/review057r2.FWMzdC/repo

/**
 * The third-party inventory: which tracked files reproduce upstream source or
 * specification text, from which project, under which licence.
 *
 * Decision request phase 1, D3 and item 5 step 1 (`REVIEW-057` R1-1). The
 * `NOTICE` is written from this tool's output, not from memory: the first
 * draft named one patch and one harness, and the records quoted a whole
 * BSD-3-Clause file nobody had counted.
 *
 * Method. Each upstream source is a CORPUS fetched at a stated version. A
 * tracked file reproduces a corpus where:
 *   - CODE: four or more substantive lines in a row (gaps of up to two
 *     non-substantive lines allowed) each appear verbatim, after trimming and
 *     collapsing whitespace, somewhere in that corpus; or
 *   - PROSE (specification and documentation corpora only): a run of 12
 *     consecutive words appears in that corpus, so a quotation that was
 *     re-wrapped or inlined is still found.
 * A substantive line has at least 20 characters after normalising and at
 * least one letter. The thresholds are a choice, printed in the output.
 *
 *   bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts            # fetch, compare, write
 *   bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts --check    # also fail if NOTICE omits a project found
 *
 * Needs network for the GitHub corpora; the crates come from the local cargo
 * registry and the npm packages from node_modules. Not part of `make ci`.
 */
import { spawnSync } from "bun";
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, relative } from "node:path";

const ROOT = join(import.meta.dir, "..");
const CACHE = process.env.WCONF_INVENTORY_CACHE ?? join(process.env.TMPDIR ?? "/tmp", "wconf-third-party-corpora");
const OUT = join(ROOT, "docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md");
const MIN_RUN = 4;
const MAX_GAP = 2;
const MIN_LINE = 20;
const SHINGLE = 12;

type Corpus = { name: string; version: string; licence: string; dir: string; prose: boolean };

function run(cmd: string[], cwd?: string): string {
  const r = spawnSync(cmd, { cwd, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd.join(" ")} failed: ${r.stderr.toString().trim()}`);
  return r.stdout.toString();
}

/** A shallow fetch of one ref of a GitHub repository into the cache. */
function github(repo: string, ref: string): string {
  const dir = join(CACHE, `${repo.replace("/", "__")}@${ref}`);
  if (existsSync(join(dir, ".done"))) return dir;
  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  run(["git", "init", "-q"], dir);
  run(["git", "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", `https://github.com/${repo}.git`, ref], dir);
  run(["git", "-c", "advice.detachedHead=false", "checkout", "-q", "FETCH_HEAD"], dir);
  writeFileSync(join(dir, ".done"), "");
  return dir;
}

/**
 * Only the files of a repository whose path matches, fetched one by one: the
 * dev portal is far too large to clone for the pages that concern this project.
 */
function pathsMatching(repo: string, ref: string, re: RegExp): Corpus {
  const dir = join(CACHE, `${repo.replace("/", "__")}@${ref}-${re.source}`);
  if (!existsSync(join(dir, ".done"))) {
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const tree = JSON.parse(run(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/git/trees/${ref}?recursive=1`]));
    if (tree.truncated) throw new Error(`${repo} tree listing is truncated; the path filter would miss files`);
    for (const e of tree.tree) {
      if (e.type !== "blob" || !re.test(e.path) || !TEXT.test(e.path)) continue;
      const body = run(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/contents/${encodeURI(e.path)}?ref=${ref}`, "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"]);
      const out = join(dir, e.path);
      mkdirSync(join(out, ".."), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(out, body);
    }
    writeFileSync(join(dir, ".done"), "");
  }
  return { name: repo, version: `${ref}, paths matching ${re}`, licence: githubLicence(repo), dir, prose: true };
}

function githubLicence(repo: string): string {
  const r = spawnSync(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/license`, "--jq", ".license.spdx_id"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  return r.exitCode === 0 ? r.stdout.toString().trim() : "no licence file found";
}

function crates(): Corpus[] {
  const lock = readFileSync(join(ROOT, "signer/Cargo.lock"), "utf8");
  const registry = join(process.env.HOME ?? "", ".cargo/registry/src");
  const indexes = existsSync(registry) ? readdirSync(registry).map((d) => join(registry, d)) : [];
  const out: Corpus[] = [];
  for (const m of lock.matchAll(/\[\[package\]\]\nname = "([^"]+)"\nversion = "([^"]+)"\nsource = "registry/g)) {
    const [, name, version] = m;
    const dir = indexes.map((i) => join(i, `${name}-${version}`)).find((d) => existsSync(d));
    if (!dir) {
      out.push({ name: `crate ${name}`, version, licence: "NOT FOUND LOCALLY — not compared", dir: "", prose: false });
      continue;
    }
    const toml = readFileSync(join(dir, "Cargo.toml"), "utf8");
    const licence = toml.match(/^license\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/m)?.[1] ?? "see crate";
    out.push({ name: `crate ${name}`, version, licence, dir, prose: false });
  }
  return out;
}

function npmPackages(): Corpus[] {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(ROOT, "package.json"), "utf8"));
  const names = [...Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}), ...Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {})];
  return names.map((name) => {
    const dir = join(ROOT, "node_modules", name);
    if (!existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) return { name: `npm ${name}`, version: "?", licence: "NOT INSTALLED — not compared", dir: "", prose: false };
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, "package.json"), "utf8"));
    return { name: `npm ${name}`, version: p.version, licence: p.license ?? "see package", dir, prose: false };
  });
}

function corpora(): Corpus[] {
  const gh = (name: string, ref: string, prose = false): Corpus => ({
    name, version: ref, licence: githubLicence(name), dir: github(name, ref), prose,
  });
  return [
    gh("XRPLF/mpt-crypto", "85dbac73d033241b73f0565ae7cce86d07005c70"),
    gh("XRPLF/mpt-crypto", "main"),
    gh("XRPLF/rippled", "3.3.0"),
    gh("XRPLF/rippled", "develop"),
    gh("XRPLF/clio", "develop"),
    gh("XRPLF/XRPL-Standards", "master", true),
    // The last XLS-0096 revision before PR #604 set it Final; quotations of the
    // older wording come from here. Resolved with `gh api`, not typed.
    gh("XRPLF/XRPL-Standards", "9fbf7ef8eb69973f43d44836875e01e6364a3ecb", true),
    // GitHub reports NOASSERTION for the dev portal, because its LICENSE also lists
    // bundled libraries. The file grants MIT for the portal's original contents
    // (read 2026-10-18).
    { ...pathsMatching("XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal", "master", /confidential/i), licence: "MIT, per its LICENSE (GitHub reports NOASSERTION)" },
    ...crates(),
    ...npmPackages(),
  ];
}

const norm = (s: string) => s.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
const substantive = (s: string) => s.length >= MIN_LINE && /[A-Za-z]/.test(s);
const TEXT = /\.(c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|ipp|rs|ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|jsx|md|txt|py|sh|toml|json|yml|yaml|cmake|in|patch|html|css)$|(^|\/)(CMakeLists\.txt|Makefile|LICENSE[^/]*)$/i;

function walk(dir: string, into: string[] = []): string[] {
  for (const e of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (e.name === ".git" || e.name === "node_modules") continue;
    const p = join(dir, e.name);
    if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p, into);
    else if (e.isFile() && TEXT.test(p) && statSync(p).size < 2_000_000) into.push(p);
  }
  return into;
}

function words(s: string): string[] {
  return s.toLowerCase().replace(/[`*_>#|\[\]()]/g, " ").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
}

/** A project is a repository, crate or package, whatever its version. */
const project = (c: Corpus) => c.name;

// line -> the projects whose corpus contains it; and the lines of licence files.
const LINES = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
const LICENCE_LINES = new Set<string>();
const SHINGLES = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
const VERSIONS = new Map<string, Set<string>>();

function index(c: Corpus): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const f of walk(c.dir)) {
    const text = readFileSync(f, "utf8");
    const isLicence = /(^|\/)(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING|NOTICE)[^/]*$/i.test(f);
    for (const l of text.split("\n")) {
      const s = norm(l);
      if (!substantive(s)) continue;
      if (isLicence) LICENCE_LINES.add(s);
      let set = LINES.get(s);
      if (!set) LINES.set(s, (set = new Set()));
      set.add(project(c));
      n++;
    }
    if (c.prose && /\.md$/i.test(f)) {
      const w = words(text);
      for (let i = 0; i + SHINGLE <= w.length; i++) {
        const k = w.slice(i, i + SHINGLE).join(" ");
        let set = SHINGLES.get(k);
        if (!set) SHINGLES.set(k, (set = new Set()));
        set.add(project(c));
      }
    }
  }
  let v = VERSIONS.get(project(c));
  if (!v) VERSIONS.set(project(c), (v = new Set()));
  v.add(c.version);
  return n;
}

type Run = { file: string; from: number; to: number; kind: "code" | "prose"; projects: string[]; lines: number };
const GENERIC_PROJECTS = 3;
const LICENCE_SHARE = 0.8;

function tracked(): string[] {
  return run(["git", "ls-files"], ROOT).split("\n").filter((f) =>
    f && TEXT.test(f) && !/(^|\/)(bun\.lock|Cargo\.lock|package-lock\.json)$/.test(f)
    && f !== "LICENSE" && f !== "NOTICE" && !f.startsWith("LICENSES/")
    && !f.startsWith("docs/third-party/") && existsSync(join(ROOT, f)));
}

/**
 * Code runs: consecutive substantive lines, with gaps of up to MAX_GAP, each
 * found in at least one corpus. A run is attributed to every project holding
 * MIN_RUN or more of its lines; it is LICENCE TEXT when most of its lines come
 * from licence files, and SHARED BOILERPLATE when more than GENERIC_PROJECTS
 * projects hold it (Cargo's generated header is in every crate).
 */
function codeRuns(file: string, raw: string[]): { attributed: Run[]; licence: Run[]; generic: Run[] } {
  const isPatch = file.endsWith(".patch");
  const lines = raw.map((l) => norm(isPatch && /^[ +-]/.test(l) && !/^(\+\+\+|---) /.test(l) ? l.slice(1) : l));
  const out = { attributed: [] as Run[], licence: [] as Run[], generic: [] as Run[] };
  let run: number[] = [];
  let gap = 0;
  const close = () => {
    if (run.length >= MIN_RUN) {
      // Only SPECIFIC lines — held by GENERIC_PROJECTS projects or fewer —
      // count toward attribution. Counting every line let a few shared
      // attributes in a long quotation push the whole of it into boilerplate,
      // and under-attributing is the unsafe direction for a notice.
      const specific = new Map<string, number>();
      const any = new Set<string>();
      let lic = 0;
      for (const i of run) {
        const held = LINES.get(lines[i])!;
        for (const p of held) any.add(p);
        if (held.size <= GENERIC_PROJECTS) for (const p of held) specific.set(p, (specific.get(p) ?? 0) + 1);
        if (LICENCE_LINES.has(lines[i])) lic++;
      }
      const projects = [...specific].filter(([, k]) => k >= MIN_RUN).map(([p]) => p).sort();
      const r: Run = { file, from: run[0] + 1, to: run[run.length - 1] + 1, kind: "code", projects: projects.length ? projects : [...any].sort(), lines: run.length };
      if (lic / run.length >= LICENCE_SHARE) out.licence.push(r);
      else if (projects.length) out.attributed.push(r);
      else if (any.size > GENERIC_PROJECTS) out.generic.push(r);
    }
    run = [];
    gap = 0;
  };
  lines.forEach((l, i) => {
    if (!substantive(l)) { if (run.length && ++gap > MAX_GAP) close(); return; }
    if (LINES.has(l)) { run.push(i); gap = 0; } else close();
  });
  close();
  return out;
}

/** Prose runs: lines carrying a SHINGLE-word run found in a prose corpus. */
function proseRuns(file: string, raw: string[]): Run[] {
  if (!file.endsWith(".md")) return [];
  const out: Run[] = [];
  raw.forEach((_, i) => {
    const w = words(raw.slice(i, i + 4).join(" "));
    const found = new Set<string>();
    for (let k = 0; k + SHINGLE <= w.length; k++) {
      const s = SHINGLES.get(w.slice(k, k + SHINGLE).join(" "));
      if (s) for (const p of s) found.add(p);
    }
    for (const p of found) {
      const prev = out.findLast((r) => r.projects[0] === p);
      if (prev && i + 1 <= prev.to + 1) { prev.to = i + 1; prev.lines++; }
      else out.push({ file, from: i + 1, to: i + 1, kind: "prose", projects: [p], lines: 1 });
    }
  });
  return out;
}

const all = corpora();
const notCompared = all.filter((c) => !c.dir);
for (const c of all) {
  if (!c.dir) continue;
  console.error(`${c.name}@${c.version}: ${index(c)} substantive lines`);
}
const LICENCE_OF = new Map(all.filter((c) => c.dir).map((c) => [project(c), c.licence]));

const attributed: Run[] = [], licenceRuns: Run[] = [], genericRuns: Run[] = [];
for (const f of tracked()) {
  const raw = readFileSync(join(ROOT, f), "utf8").split("\n");
  const r = codeRuns(f, raw);
  attributed.push(...r.attributed, ...proseRuns(f, raw));
  licenceRuns.push(...r.licence);
  genericRuns.push(...r.generic);
}

const byProject = new Map<string, Run[]>();
for (const r of attributed) for (const p of r.projects) {
  if (!byProject.has(p)) byProject.set(p, []);
  byProject.get(p)!.push(r);
}
const range = (r: Run) => (r.from === r.to ? `${r.from}` : `${r.from}–${r.to}`);
const table = (runs: Run[], withProjects: boolean) => {
  const byFile = new Map<string, Run[]>();
  for (const r of runs) { if (!byFile.has(r.file)) byFile.set(r.file, []); byFile.get(r.file)!.push(r); }
  let s = withProjects ? "| file | lines | shared by |\n|---|---|---|\n" : "| file | kind | lines |\n|---|---|---|\n";
  for (const [f, rs] of byFile) {
    s += withProjects
      ? `| \`${f}\` | ${rs.map(range).join(", ")} | ${[...new Set(rs.flatMap((r) => r.projects))].length} projects |\n`
      : `| \`${f}\` | ${[...new Set(rs.map((r) => r.kind))].join(", ")} | ${rs.map(range).join(", ")} |\n`;
  }
  return s;
};

let md = `# Third-party inventory

⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with \`bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts\`.

Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. \`NOTICE\` is
written from this file. Method: code is **${MIN_RUN} or more substantive lines in a row**,
with gaps of up to ${MAX_GAP}, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
is attributed to every project holding ${MIN_RUN} or more of the run's lines; prose is
**a run of ${SHINGLE} consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
corpora only. A substantive line has ${MIN_LINE} or more characters and a letter. A run
is **licence text** when ${LICENCE_SHARE * 100}% of its lines come from licence files, and
**shared boilerplate** when more than ${GENERIC_PROJECTS} projects hold it; neither is
attributed, and only lines held by ${GENERIC_PROJECTS} projects or fewer count toward
attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
which are PDFs under \`docs/references/\` and not in version control;
\`bitcoin-core/secp256k1\`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
documentation. \`LICENSE\`, \`NOTICE\` and
\`LICENSES/\` are not compared.

**${all.length} corpora in ${VERSIONS.size} projects compared; ${byProject.size} projects reproduced; ${notCompared.length} corpora not compared.**

`;
for (const [p, runs] of [...byProject].sort()) {
  md += `## ${p} — ${LICENCE_OF.get(p)}\n\nCompared at ${[...VERSIONS.get(p)!].map((v) => `\`${v}\``).join(", ")}.\n\n${table(runs, false)}\n`;
}
md += `## Licence text, not attributed\n\n${licenceRuns.length ? table(licenceRuns, true) : "None.\n"}\n`;
md += `## Shared boilerplate, not attributed\n\n${genericRuns.length ? table(genericRuns, true) : "None.\n"}\n`;
if (notCompared.length) {
  md += `## Not compared\n\n${notCompared.map((c) => `- ${c.name} \`${c.version}\`: ${c.licence}`).join("\n")}\n`;
}
mkdirSync(join(ROOT, "docs/third-party"), { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(OUT, md);
console.log(`wrote ${relative(ROOT, OUT)} — ${byProject.size} projects reproduced, ${licenceRuns.length} licence-text and ${genericRuns.length} boilerplate runs set aside`);
const found = [...byProject.keys()];

if (process.argv.includes("--check")) {
  const notice = existsSync(join(ROOT, "NOTICE")) ? readFileSync(join(ROOT, "NOTICE"), "utf8") : "";
  const missing = found.map((p) => p.replace(/^(crate|npm) /, "")).filter((n) => !notice.includes(n));
  if (missing.length) {
    console.log(`check: FAIL — NOTICE does not name: ${missing.join(", ")}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log("check: PASS — NOTICE names every project with a hit");
}
# Third-party inventory

⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with `bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts`.

Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. `NOTICE` is
written from this file. Method: code is **4 or more substantive lines in a row**,
with gaps of up to 2, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
is attributed to every project holding 4 or more of the run's lines; prose is
**a run of 12 consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
corpora only. A substantive line has 20 or more characters and a letter. A run
is **licence text** when 80% of its lines come from licence files, and
**shared boilerplate** when more than 3 projects hold it; neither is
attributed, and only lines held by 3 projects or fewer count toward
attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
which are PDFs under `docs/references/` and not in version control;
`bitcoin-core/secp256k1`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
documentation. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and
`LICENSES/` are not compared.

**108 corpora in 91 projects compared; 6 projects reproduced; 14 corpora not compared.**

xrpl-confidential-positions
Copyright 2026 Nandan

Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (see LICENSE).

This repository reproduces material that third parties own. That material is
NOT covered by the Apache License: it stays under its owners' terms, set out
below. docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md lists every file and line range found,
the versions compared and how they were found, and
tools/inventory-third-party.ts rebuilds it. What that search cannot see is
stated at its head.

1. XRPLF/mpt-crypto, which carries no licence

   - tools/spike-2026-08-18/wconf-nonces.patch is a patch against
     XRPLF/mpt-crypto at 85dbac7. Its context lines and removed lines, 841 in
     all, are upstream source.
   - tools/mpt-crypto-bench/wconf_bench.c lifts proof setup code from
     mpt-crypto's tests at the same commit.
   - Some review records under docs/reviews/ quote its source.

   XRPLF/mpt-crypto carried no licence file at that commit or at main when
   checked on 2026-10-18. The npm package @xrplf/mpt-crypto is ISC-licensed;
   it ships a WASM build and no C source, and this repository does not treat
   its licence as a grant for the C source. The upstream lines are not
   relicensed here. They are reproduced so that the signer can be rebuilt and
   the review records can be checked, and they will be removed if the
   copyright holder asks.

2. Material under licences that require their notice to travel with copies.
   Each notice is reproduced verbatim in LICENSES/.

   - ed25519-dalek 2.2.0, BSD-3-Clause: source quoted in review records under
     docs/reviews/. LICENSES/ed25519-dalek-BSD-3-Clause.txt
   - XRPLF/rippled, ISC: source quoted in review records, research notes and an
     upstream filing draft. LICENSES/rippled-ISC.md
   - XRPLF/XRPL-Standards, MIT: specification text, XLS-0096 among it, quoted
     in the claims register, review records, research notes and filing drafts.
     LICENSES/XRPL-Standards-MIT.txt
   - XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal, MIT for its original contents: documentation text
     quoted in the feedback register, review records and filing drafts.
     LICENSES/xrpl-dev-portal-MIT.txt
   - ripple-binary-codec 2.9.0, ISC: lines in a test-vector file under
     tools/spike-step3-2026-08-18/. LICENSES/ripple-binary-codec-ISC.txt

The packages this repository depends on are installed by bun and cargo at
build time and are not redistributed here, except as listed above.

+### D8. What keeps the private history out of the public repository
+
+**Context.** `REVIEW-057` R1-3, upheld in part. A `pre-push` hook is not a

+machine only: every repository under the home directory's project folders and the
+temporary directories, searched to depth 7, was tested for the private history's
+root commit `b71638c`. Seven hold it. **This checkout** has the guard. **Six are
+scratch clones** in the temporary directory, from `REVIEW-056`'s and `REVIEW-057`'s
+legs and an earlier CI rehearsal; none has a GitHub remote, so none can make the

+sessions. A second search then found the private history in this checkout only.
+
+**Why A.** The route that exists in practice is a clone whose `origin` still names
+the old repository, and the inventory and the guard close it. B and C close the
+rest at a standing cost to every later change, for a single-maintainer research
+repository. **If you want the boundary rather than the guard, B is the cheaper of
+the two.**

+# Third-party inventory
+
+⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with `bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts`.
+
+Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. `NOTICE` is
+written from this file. Method: code is **4 or more substantive lines in a row**,
+with gaps of up to 2, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
+is attributed to every project holding 4 or more of the run's lines; prose is
+**a run of 12 consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
+corpora only. A substantive line has 20 or more characters and a letter. A run
+is **licence text** when 80% of its lines come from licence files, and
+**shared boilerplate** when more than 3 projects hold it; neither is
+attributed, and only lines held by 3 projects or fewer count toward
+attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
+paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
+cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
+which are PDFs under `docs/references/` and not in version control;
+`bitcoin-core/secp256k1`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
+documentation. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and
+`LICENSES/` are not compared.
+
+**108 corpora in 91 projects compared; 6 projects reproduced; 14 corpora not compared.**
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Self-test for the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push.
+#
+# Every case runs against the real hook, installed by the real installer into a
+# throwaway repository, with a fake `gh` on PATH so nothing touches GitHub.
+# Then every case runs again against MUTANTS of the hook, each of which removes
+# one protection. A mutant that the cases do not catch fails this check, and so
+# does a mutation that does not apply: a case list that a broken hook still
+# passes proves nothing.
+#
+# Needs bash, git and perl. No network.
+set -u
+
+top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
+HOOK_SRC="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
+INSTALL_SRC="$top/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
+work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/push-guard.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+G() {
+  git -c user.name=guard -c user.email=guard@example.invalid \
+      -c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false -c init.defaultBranch=main "$@"
+}
+ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
+FAILED=0
+fail() { printf '  ✗ %s\n' "$1"; FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); }
+pass() { printf '  ✓ %s\n' "$1"; }
+
+if hp=$(git config --global --get core.hooksPath); then
+  printf 'check-push-guard: FAIL — core.hooksPath is set globally (%s), so the guard cannot run on this machine\n' "$hp"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# --- a fake gh, answering `gh api repos/<owner>/<name> --jq <expr>` from a table
+mkdir -p "$work/bin" "$work/minbin"
+cat >"$work/bin/gh" <<'EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+[ "${1-}" = api ] || exit 2
+want=$(printf '%s' "${2#repos/}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
+while read -r name id private; do
+  if [ "$(printf '%s' "$name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" = "$want" ]; then
+    case "${4-}" in
+      *full_name*) printf '%s %s %s\n' "$id" "$private" "$name" ;;
+      *) printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$private" ;;
+    esac
+    exit 0
+  fi
+done <"$FAKE_GH_TABLE"
+echo 'HTTP 404: Not Found' >&2
+exit 1
+EOF
+chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
+for t in bash git tr; do ln -s "$(command -v "$t")" "$work/minbin/$t"; done
+PATH_GH="$work/bin:$PATH"
+PATH_NO_GH="$work/minbin"
+
+TABLE="$work/table"
+printf 'arch/ive 100 true\npub/lic 200 true\nflip/ped 300 false\n' >"$TABLE"
+TABLE_FLIPPED="$work/table-flipped"
+printf 'arch/ive 100 false\npub/lic 200 true\n' >"$TABLE_FLIPPED"
+
+# --- the "private" clone: a history with one root, then the guard installed
+P="$work/private"
+G init -q "$P"
+G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
+G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m second
+ROOT=$(G -C "$P" rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)
+PRIV=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)
+mkdir -p "$P/tools/git-hooks"
+cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
+cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$P/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
+G -C "$P" remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git
+
+echo "The installer:"
+if out=$(cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1); then
+  pass "installs against a private archive"
+else
+  fail "installs against a private archive: $out"
+fi
+[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid)" = 100 ] \
+  && pass "records the archive's repository id" || fail "records the archive's repository id"
+[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.roots)" = "$ROOT" ] \
+  && pass "records the history's root" || fail "records the history's root"
+cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push" \
+  && pass "copies the hook byte for byte" || fail "copies the hook byte for byte"
+
+installer_refuses() { # <label> <needle> <setup...>
+  local label=$1 needle=$2 d="$work/inst.$RANDOM"
+  shift 2
+  G init -q "$d" && G -C "$d" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
+  mkdir -p "$d/tools/git-hooks"
+  cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$d/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
+  cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$d/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
+  (cd "$d" && "$@")
+  local o rc
+  o=$(cd "$d" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1)
+  rc=$?
+  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "$o" | grep -qF "$needle"; then pass "$label"; else fail "$label (exit $rc): $o"; fi
+}
+installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not private" "is not private" \
+  git remote add origin https://github.com/flip/ped.git
+installer_refuses "refuses when core.hooksPath is set" "core.hooksPath is set" \
+  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && git config core.hooksPath .hooks'
+installer_refuses "refuses to overwrite a foreign pre-push hook" "is not this guard" \
+  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && printf "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n" > .git/hooks/pre-push'
+installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not on GitHub" "not a GitHub repository" \
+  git remote add origin "$work/somewhere.git"
+
+# History created AFTER the install, as it would be in the real clone.
+G -C "$P" tag -a -m t ptag "$PRIV"
+TAGOBJ=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse ptag)
+G -C "$P" checkout -q --orphan clean
+G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m orphan
+ORPH=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)
+G -C "$P" checkout -q main
+
+# A clone with the hook but no configuration, and one whose recorded root is absent.
+U="$work/unconfigured"
+G init -q "$U" && G -C "$U" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
+cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$U/.git/hooks/pre-push"
+S="$work/shallow"
+G init -q "$S" && G -C "$S" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
+cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$S/.git/hooks/pre-push"
+G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.archiveid 100
+G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.roots 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
+
+ref() { printf 'refs/heads/main %s refs/heads/main %s\n' "$1" "$ZERO"; }
+
+# One case: <name> <0|1> <needle or -> <url> <stdin> [repo] [PATH] [table]
+case_result() {
+  local name=$1 want=$2 needle=$3 url=$4 input=$5 repo=${6:-$P} path=${7:-$PATH_GH} table=${8:-$TABLE}
+  local out rc
+  out=$(cd "$repo" && printf '%s' "$input" | PATH="$path" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$table" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push" origin "$url" 2>&1)
+  rc=$?
+  if [ "$want" = 0 ]; then
+    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]
+  else
+    [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && { [ "$needle" = - ] || printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF "$needle"; }
+  fi
+}
+
+NOT_ARCHIVE="is not the archive"
+NOT_GITHUB="is not a GitHub repository"
+CASES=(
+  "A1|0|-|https://github.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
+  "A2|0|-|git@github.com:arch/ive.git|PRIV"
+  "A3|0|-|https://GITHUB.COM/Arch/Ive.git/|PRIV"
+  "A4|0|-|ssh://ssh.github.com:443/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
+  "R1|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV"
+  "R2|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|git@github.com:pub/lic.git|PRIV"
+  "R3|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|ssh://git@github.com/pub/lic|PRIV"
+  "R4|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/PUB/LIC.git/|PRIV"
+  "R5|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://git@github.com/pub/lic|PRIV"
+  "R6|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic//|PRIV"
+  "R7|1|$NOT_GITHUB|$work/public.git|PRIV"
+  "R8|1|$NOT_GITHUB|file://$work/public.git|PRIV"
+  "R9|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com.example.org/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
+  "R10|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://example.org/github.com/arch/ive|PRIV"
+  "R11|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://gitlab.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
+  "R12|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com/arch/ive/extra|PRIV"
+  "R13|1|could not be read|https://github.com/no/such|PRIV"
+  "R14|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|TAG"
+  "R15|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|MIXED"
+  "R16|1|gh is not on PATH|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|NOGH"
+  "R17|1|is not private|https://github.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV|FLIPPED"
+  "R18|1|not configured|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|UNCONF"
+  "R19|1|is not in this clone|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|SHALLOW"
+  "O1|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|ORPH"
+  "O2|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|DELETE"
+  "O3|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|EMPTY"
+)
+CASE_COUNT=${#CASES[@]}
+
+# Runs every case; prints the names that fail, one per line.
+run_cases() {
+  local c name want needle url what mode input repo path table
+  for c in "${CASES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r name want needle url what mode <<<"$c"
+    repo=$P path=$PATH_GH table=$TABLE
+    case "$what" in
+      PRIV) input=$(ref "$PRIV") ;;
+      TAG) input=$(printf 'refs/tags/ptag %s refs/tags/ptag %s\n' "$TAGOBJ" "$ZERO") ;;
+      MIXED) input=$(ref "$ORPH"; printf 'refs/heads/two %s refs/heads/two %s\n' "$PRIV" "$ZERO") ;;
+      ORPH) input=$(ref "$ORPH") ;;
+      DELETE) input=$(printf '(delete) %s refs/heads/old %s\n' "$ZERO" "$PRIV") ;;
+      EMPTY) input= ;;
+    esac
+    case "${mode-}" in
+      NOGH) path=$PATH_NO_GH ;;
+      FLIPPED) table=$TABLE_FLIPPED ;;
+      UNCONF) repo=$U ;;
+      SHALLOW) repo=$S ;;
+    esac
+    case_result "$name" "$want" "$needle" "$url" "$input" "$repo" "$path" "$table" || echo "$name"
+  done
+}
+
+echo
+echo "The hook, ${CASE_COUNT} cases:"
+failed_cases=$(run_cases)
+if [ -z "$failed_cases" ]; then
+  pass "all ${CASE_COUNT} cases"
+else
+  for n in $failed_cases; do fail "case $n"; done
+fi
+
+echo
+echo "Through git itself:"
+G init -q --bare "$work/public.git"
+if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
+  fail "a real push of the private history is refused"
+else
+  G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/main >/dev/null \
+    && fail "a real push of the private history is refused (but the ref arrived)" \
+    || pass "a real push of the private history is refused, and nothing arrives"
+fi
+if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" clean 2>/dev/null) \
+   && [ "$(G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse refs/heads/clean)" = "$ORPH" ]; then
+  pass "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
+else
+  fail "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
+fi
+if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q --dry-run "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
+  fail "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
+else
+  pass "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
+fi
+
+# --- mutants: each removes one protection, and the named case must catch it
+echo
+echo "Mutants — each must be caught by the case named:"
+# Four parallel arrays, because several patterns contain `|`.
+M_MUST=() M_LABEL=() M_FROM=() M_TO=()
+mutant() { M_MUST+=("$1"); M_LABEL+=("$2"); M_FROM+=("$3"); M_TO+=("$4"); }
+mutant R1 "ancestry not detected" '0) carries=1; break 2 ;;' '0) ;;'
+mutant R1 "every ref skipped" 'case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac' 'continue'
+mutant R1 "repository id not compared" '[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ]' 'true'
+mutant R9 "host matched loosely" 'github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;' '*github.com*) ;;'
+mutant R12 "extra path segments accepted" "*/*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;" "/* | */ | '') return 1 ;;"
+mutant R13 "fail-open when GitHub cannot be read" '|| refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"' '|| exit 0'
+mutant R15 "only the first pushed ref read" 'while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' 'read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; for _once in 1; do'
+mutant R1 "a last line with no newline dropped" ' || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' '; do'
+mutant R17 "archive's visibility not checked" '[ "$private" = "true" ]' 'true'
+mutant R18 "unconfigured clone allowed" 'refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"' 'exit 0'
+mutant R19 "absent root not refused" '|| refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"' '|| true'
+MUTANT_COUNT=${#M_MUST[@]}
+# A mutant counts as caught only if its case passed on the real hook. If the real
+# hook fails any case, every mutant would look caught, so none is evaluated.
+if [ -n "$failed_cases" ]; then
+  fail "no mutant evaluated: the real hook fails cases, so a mutant's failures would prove nothing"
+  M_MUST=()
+fi
+for i in "${!M_MUST[@]}"; do
+  must=${M_MUST[$i]} label=${M_LABEL[$i]}
+  for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do
+    cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
+    FROM=${M_FROM[$i]} TO=${M_TO[$i]} perl -0pi -e 's/\Q$ENV{FROM}\E/$ENV{TO}/' "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
+  done
+  if cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push"; then
+    fail "mutant '$label' did not apply — the pattern no longer matches the hook"
+    continue
+  fi
+  caught=$(run_cases)
+  if printf '%s\n' "$caught" | grep -qx "$must"; then
+    pass "'$label' is caught by $must"
+  else
+    fail "'$label' is NOT caught by $must (cases failing: $(printf '%s' "$caught" | tr '\n' ' '))"
+  fi
+done
+for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"; done
+
+echo
+echo "What this does not check:"
+echo "  1. git push --no-verify, which skips every hook; a clone the guard was never"
+echo "     installed in; and core.hooksPath set after the install."
+echo "  2. Real GitHub. gh is faked here. make install-push-guard reads the real"
+echo "     archive, and a git push --dry-run to a real public repository proves the"
+echo "     refusal without sending anything."
+echo "  3. The hook treats a merge-base error as carrying the private history. No case"
+echo "     produces that error, so that branch has no mutant."
+echo
+if [ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]; then
+  printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=PASS cases=%d mutants=%d exit=0\n' "$CASE_COUNT" "$MUTANT_COUNT"
+  exit 0
+fi
+printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=FAIL failures=%d exit=1\n' "$FAILED"
+exit 1

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# wconf push guard — the pre-push hook for this repository's PRIVATE clones.
+#
+# Decision request phase 1, D4. Installed by `make install-push-guard`, which
+# copies this file into the clone's hooks directory and records two values in
+# the clone's git config: the private archive's GitHub repository id, and the
+# root commits of the private history.
+#
+# The property: a push that carries the private history goes to the private
+# archive and nowhere else. "Carries" means a pushed commit has a recorded root
+# as an ancestor. "The archive" means the destination's GitHub repository id
+# equals the recorded one and GitHub reports it private. The id survives a
+# rename, so the check holds before the rename, after it, and while the new
+# public repository is still private, which a visibility check alone would not.
+#
+# Measured on git 2.50.1 before this was written: git passes the destination
+# AFTER `insteadOf`, `pushInsteadOf` and `pushurl` are applied, and runs the
+# hook once for every push URL of a remote.
+#
+# ⚠ A guard against mistakes, not against the owner. `git push --no-verify`
+# skips it, and it does nothing in a clone it was never installed in.
+#
+# `make check-push-guard` breaks it every way it knows and fails if any break
+# goes unnoticed.
+set -u
+
+# Prints `owner/name` for a GitHub URL, or fails. Hosts are matched exactly, so
+# `github.com.example.org` is not GitHub.
+parse_github_url() {
+  local u=$1 rest hostpart host path
+  case "$u" in
+    https://* | http://* | ssh://* | git://*)
+      rest=${u#*://}
+      hostpart=${rest%%/*}
+      [ "$hostpart" = "$rest" ] && return 1
+      path=${rest#*/}
+      ;;
+    *:*)
+      # scp-like `[user@]host:path`, which git takes only when no `/` comes
+      # before the first `:`.
+      hostpart=${u%%:*}
+      case "$hostpart" in */*) return 1 ;; esac
+      path=${u#*:}
+      ;;
+    *) return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  hostpart=${hostpart##*@}
+  host=$(printf '%s' "${hostpart%%:*}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
+  case "$host" in
+    github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;
+    *) return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
+  path=${path%.git}
+  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
+  case "$path" in
+    */*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;
+    ?*/?*) ;;
+    *) return 1 ;;
+  esac
+  printf '%s\n' "$path"
+}
+
+if [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && [ "$1" = "--parse-url" ]; then
+  parse_github_url "$2"
+  exit
+fi
+
+url=${2-}
+refuse() {
+  printf 'push guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2
+  printf '  destination: %s\n' "$url" >&2
+  printf '  This history may go only to the private archive. Publish from the\n' >&2
+  printf '  export instead: decision request phase 1, item 5, step 4.\n' >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+roots=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.roots || true)
+archive_id=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid || true)
+if [ -z "$roots" ] || [ -z "$archive_id" ]; then
+  refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"
+fi
+for r in $roots; do
+  git cat-file -e "${r}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
+    || refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"
+done
+
+carries=0
+# `|| [ -n … ]` keeps a last line with no newline. git always sends one; the
+# guard should not depend on it.
+while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do
+  [ -n "${local_sha-}" ] || continue
+  # A deletion publishes nothing.
+  case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
+  if ! commit=$(git rev-parse -q --verify "${local_sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null); then
+    carries=1
+    break
+  fi
+  for r in $roots; do
+    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$r" "$commit" 2>/dev/null
+    case $? in
+      0) carries=1; break 2 ;;
+      1) ;;
+      *) carries=1; break 2 ;;
+    esac
+  done
+done
+[ "$carries" = 0 ] && exit 0
+
+target=$(parse_github_url "$url") \
+  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and the destination is not a GitHub repository"
+command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and gh is not on PATH, so the destination cannot be checked"
+info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private)"' 2>/dev/null) \
+  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"
+id=${info%% *}
+private=${info#* }
+[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ] \
+  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and $target (repository id $id) is not the archive (id $archive_id)"
+[ "$private" = "true" ] \
+  || refuse "$target is the archive, but GitHub reports that it is not private"
+exit 0
