+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Installs the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push, in this clone.
+#
+# Run it in every PRIVATE clone (decision request phase 1, D4 and item 5,
+# step 8). It records the archive as the GitHub repository behind the clone's
+# own push URL — so run it while `origin` is the private archive, under either
+# name — and refuses if GitHub does not report that repository private.
+#
+# The hook is COPIED, not linked. A link into the tracked file would vanish on
+# checking out any commit that predates it, and git treats a missing hook as
+# no hook.
+#
+# Usage: tools/install-push-guard.sh [remote]   (default: origin)
+set -euo pipefail
+
+fail() { printf 'install-push-guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
+src="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
+[ -f "$src" ] || fail "$src is missing"
+
+if hooks_path=$(git config --get core.hooksPath); then
+  fail "core.hooksPath is set ($hooks_path), so a hook copied into the hooks directory would not run"
+fi
+hooks_dir=$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)
+case "$hooks_dir" in /*) ;; *) hooks_dir="$top/$hooks_dir" ;; esac
+dest="$hooks_dir/pre-push"
+if [ -e "$dest" ] && ! grep -q '^# wconf push guard' "$dest"; then
+  fail "$dest exists and is not this guard; move it aside first"
+fi
+
+remote=${1:-origin}
+push_url=$(git remote get-url --push "$remote") || fail "no remote named $remote"
+target=$(bash "$src" --parse-url "$push_url") \
+  || fail "$remote's push URL is not a GitHub repository: $push_url"
+command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "gh is not on PATH"
+info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private) \(.full_name)"') \
+  || fail "could not read repos/$target from GitHub"
+read -r archive_id private full_name <<<"$info"
+[ "$private" = "true" ] || fail "$full_name is not private, so it cannot be the archive"
+
+roots=$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
+roots=${roots% }
+[ -n "$roots" ] || fail "this clone has no commits"
+
+git config wconf.pushguard.archiveid "$archive_id"
+git config wconf.pushguard.archivename "$full_name"
+git config wconf.pushguard.roots "$roots"
+mkdir -p "$hooks_dir"
+cp "$src" "$dest"
+chmod 0755 "$dest"
+
+printf 'push guard installed: %s\n' "$dest"
+printf '  archive: %s (repository id %s, private)\n' "$full_name" "$archive_id"
+printf '  roots:   %s\n' "$roots"
+printf '  A push carrying a commit with one of those roots may go only to that\n'
+printf '  repository id. It does not run on git push --no-verify, in a clone it\n'
+printf '  was never installed in, or if core.hooksPath is set later.\n'

+/**
+ * The third-party inventory: which tracked files reproduce upstream source or
+ * specification text, from which project, under which licence.
+ *
+ * Decision request phase 1, D3 and item 5 step 1 (`REVIEW-057` R1-1). The
+ * `NOTICE` is written from this tool's output, not from memory: the first
+ * draft named one patch and one harness, and the records quoted a whole
+ * BSD-3-Clause file nobody had counted.
+ *
+ * Method. Each upstream source is a CORPUS fetched at a stated version. A
+ * tracked file reproduces a corpus where:
+ *   - CODE: four or more substantive lines in a row (gaps of up to two
+ *     non-substantive lines allowed) each appear verbatim, after trimming and
+ *     collapsing whitespace, somewhere in that corpus; or
+ *   - PROSE (specification and documentation corpora only): a run of 12
+ *     consecutive words appears in that corpus, so a quotation that was
+ *     re-wrapped or inlined is still found.
+ * A substantive line has at least 20 characters after normalising and at
+ * least one letter. The thresholds are a choice, printed in the output.
+ *
+ *   bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts            # fetch, compare, write
+ *   bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts --check    # also fail if NOTICE omits a project found
+ *
+ * Needs network for the GitHub corpora; the crates come from the local cargo
+ * registry and the npm packages from node_modules. Not part of `make ci`.
+ */
+import { spawnSync } from "bun";
+import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { join, relative } from "node:path";
+
+const ROOT = join(import.meta.dir, "..");
+const CACHE = process.env.WCONF_INVENTORY_CACHE ?? join(process.env.TMPDIR ?? "/tmp", "wconf-third-party-corpora");
+const OUT = join(ROOT, "docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md");
+const MIN_RUN = 4;
+const MAX_GAP = 2;
+const MIN_LINE = 20;
+const SHINGLE = 12;
+
+type Corpus = { name: string; version: string; licence: string; dir: string; prose: boolean };
+
+function run(cmd: string[], cwd?: string): string {
+  const r = spawnSync(cmd, { cwd, stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`${cmd.join(" ")} failed: ${r.stderr.toString().trim()}`);
+  return r.stdout.toString();
+}
+
+/** A shallow fetch of one ref of a GitHub repository into the cache. */
+function github(repo: string, ref: string): string {
+  const dir = join(CACHE, `${repo.replace("/", "__")}@${ref}`);
+  if (existsSync(join(dir, ".done"))) return dir;
+  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
+  run(["git", "init", "-q"], dir);
+  run(["git", "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", `https://github.com/${repo}.git`, ref], dir);
+  run(["git", "-c", "advice.detachedHead=false", "checkout", "-q", "FETCH_HEAD"], dir);
+  writeFileSync(join(dir, ".done"), "");
+  return dir;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Only the files of a repository whose path matches, fetched one by one: the
+ * dev portal is far too large to clone for the pages that concern this project.
+ */
+function pathsMatching(repo: string, ref: string, re: RegExp): Corpus {
+  const dir = join(CACHE, `${repo.replace("/", "__")}@${ref}-${re.source}`);
+  if (!existsSync(join(dir, ".done"))) {
+    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
+    const tree = JSON.parse(run(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/git/trees/${ref}?recursive=1`]));
+    if (tree.truncated) throw new Error(`${repo} tree listing is truncated; the path filter would miss files`);
+    for (const e of tree.tree) {
+      if (e.type !== "blob" || !re.test(e.path) || !TEXT.test(e.path)) continue;
+      const body = run(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/contents/${encodeURI(e.path)}?ref=${ref}`, "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"]);
+      const out = join(dir, e.path);
+      mkdirSync(join(out, ".."), { recursive: true });
+      writeFileSync(out, body);
+    }
+    writeFileSync(join(dir, ".done"), "");
+  }
+  return { name: repo, version: `${ref}, paths matching ${re}`, licence: githubLicence(repo), dir, prose: true };
+}
+
+function githubLicence(repo: string): string {
+  const r = spawnSync(["gh", "api", `repos/${repo}/license`, "--jq", ".license.spdx_id"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
+  return r.exitCode === 0 ? r.stdout.toString().trim() : "no licence file found";
+}
+
+function crates(): Corpus[] {
+  const lock = readFileSync(join(ROOT, "signer/Cargo.lock"), "utf8");
+  const registry = join(process.env.HOME ?? "", ".cargo/registry/src");
+  const indexes = existsSync(registry) ? readdirSync(registry).map((d) => join(registry, d)) : [];
+  const out: Corpus[] = [];
+  for (const m of lock.matchAll(/\[\[package\]\]\nname = "([^"]+)"\nversion = "([^"]+)"\nsource = "registry/g)) {
+    const [, name, version] = m;
+    const dir = indexes.map((i) => join(i, `${name}-${version}`)).find((d) => existsSync(d));
+    if (!dir) {
+      out.push({ name: `crate ${name}`, version, licence: "NOT FOUND LOCALLY — not compared", dir: "", prose: false });
+      continue;
+    }
+    const toml = readFileSync(join(dir, "Cargo.toml"), "utf8");
+    const licence = toml.match(/^license\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/m)?.[1] ?? "see crate";
+    out.push({ name: `crate ${name}`, version, licence, dir, prose: false });
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+
+function npmPackages(): Corpus[] {
+  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(ROOT, "package.json"), "utf8"));
+  const names = [...Object.keys(pkg.dependencies ?? {}), ...Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies ?? {})];
+  return names.map((name) => {
+    const dir = join(ROOT, "node_modules", name);
+    if (!existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) return { name: `npm ${name}`, version: "?", licence: "NOT INSTALLED — not compared", dir: "", prose: false };
+    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, "package.json"), "utf8"));
+    return { name: `npm ${name}`, version: p.version, licence: p.license ?? "see package", dir, prose: false };
+  });
+}
+
+function corpora(): Corpus[] {
+  const gh = (name: string, ref: string, prose = false): Corpus => ({
+    name, version: ref, licence: githubLicence(name), dir: github(name, ref), prose,
+  });
+  return [
+    gh("XRPLF/mpt-crypto", "85dbac73d033241b73f0565ae7cce86d07005c70"),
+    gh("XRPLF/mpt-crypto", "main"),
+    gh("XRPLF/rippled", "3.3.0"),
+    gh("XRPLF/rippled", "develop"),
+    gh("XRPLF/clio", "develop"),
+    gh("XRPLF/XRPL-Standards", "master", true),
+    // The last XLS-0096 revision before PR #604 set it Final; quotations of the
+    // older wording come from here. Resolved with `gh api`, not typed.
+    gh("XRPLF/XRPL-Standards", "9fbf7ef8eb69973f43d44836875e01e6364a3ecb", true),
+    // GitHub reports NOASSERTION for the dev portal, because its LICENSE also lists
+    // bundled libraries. The file grants MIT for the portal's original contents
+    // (read 2026-10-18).
+    { ...pathsMatching("XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal", "master", /confidential/i), licence: "MIT, per its LICENSE (GitHub reports NOASSERTION)" },
+    ...crates(),
+    ...npmPackages(),
+  ];
+}
+
+const norm = (s: string) => s.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ");
+const substantive = (s: string) => s.length >= MIN_LINE && /[A-Za-z]/.test(s);
+const TEXT = /\.(c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|ipp|rs|ts|tsx|js|mjs|cjs|jsx|md|txt|py|sh|toml|json|yml|yaml|cmake|in|patch|html|css)$|(^|\/)(CMakeLists\.txt|Makefile|LICENSE[^/]*)$/i;
+
+function walk(dir: string, into: string[] = []): string[] {
+  for (const e of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
+    if (e.name === ".git" || e.name === "node_modules") continue;
+    const p = join(dir, e.name);
+    if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p, into);
+    else if (e.isFile() && TEXT.test(p) && statSync(p).size < 2_000_000) into.push(p);
+  }
+  return into;
+}
+
+function words(s: string): string[] {
+  return s.toLowerCase().replace(/[`*_>#|\[\]()]/g, " ").split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
+}
+
+/** A project is a repository, crate or package, whatever its version. */
+const project = (c: Corpus) => c.name;
+
+// line -> the projects whose corpus contains it; and the lines of licence files.
+const LINES = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
+const LICENCE_LINES = new Set<string>();
+const SHINGLES = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
+const VERSIONS = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
+
+function index(c: Corpus): number {
+  let n = 0;
+  for (const f of walk(c.dir)) {
+    const text = readFileSync(f, "utf8");
+    const isLicence = /(^|\/)(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING|NOTICE)[^/]*$/i.test(f);
+    for (const l of text.split("\n")) {
+      const s = norm(l);
+      if (!substantive(s)) continue;
+      if (isLicence) LICENCE_LINES.add(s);
+      let set = LINES.get(s);
+      if (!set) LINES.set(s, (set = new Set()));
+      set.add(project(c));
+      n++;
+    }
+    if (c.prose && /\.md$/i.test(f)) {
+      const w = words(text);
+      for (let i = 0; i + SHINGLE <= w.length; i++) {
+        const k = w.slice(i, i + SHINGLE).join(" ");
+        let set = SHINGLES.get(k);
+        if (!set) SHINGLES.set(k, (set = new Set()));
+        set.add(project(c));
+      }
+    }
+  }
+  let v = VERSIONS.get(project(c));
+  if (!v) VERSIONS.set(project(c), (v = new Set()));
+  v.add(c.version);
+  return n;
+}
+
+type Run = { file: string; from: number; to: number; kind: "code" | "prose"; projects: string[]; lines: number };
+const GENERIC_PROJECTS = 3;
+const LICENCE_SHARE = 0.8;
+
+function tracked(): string[] {
+  return run(["git", "ls-files"], ROOT).split("\n").filter((f) =>
+    f && TEXT.test(f) && !/(^|\/)(bun\.lock|Cargo\.lock|package-lock\.json)$/.test(f)
+    && f !== "LICENSE" && f !== "NOTICE" && !f.startsWith("LICENSES/")
+    && !f.startsWith("docs/third-party/") && existsSync(join(ROOT, f)));
+}
+
+/**
+ * Code runs: consecutive substantive lines, with gaps of up to MAX_GAP, each
+ * found in at least one corpus. A run is attributed to every project holding
+ * MIN_RUN or more of its lines; it is LICENCE TEXT when most of its lines come
+ * from licence files, and SHARED BOILERPLATE when more than GENERIC_PROJECTS
+ * projects hold it (Cargo's generated header is in every crate).
+ */
+function codeRuns(file: string, raw: string[]): { attributed: Run[]; licence: Run[]; generic: Run[] } {
+  const isPatch = file.endsWith(".patch");
+  const lines = raw.map((l) => norm(isPatch && /^[ +-]/.test(l) && !/^(\+\+\+|---) /.test(l) ? l.slice(1) : l));
+  const out = { attributed: [] as Run[], licence: [] as Run[], generic: [] as Run[] };
+  let run: number[] = [];
+  let gap = 0;
+  const close = () => {
+    if (run.length >= MIN_RUN) {
+      // Only SPECIFIC lines — held by GENERIC_PROJECTS projects or fewer —
+      // count toward attribution. Counting every line let a few shared
+      // attributes in a long quotation push the whole of it into boilerplate,
+      // and under-attributing is the unsafe direction for a notice.
+      const specific = new Map<string, number>();
+      const any = new Set<string>();
+      let lic = 0;
+      for (const i of run) {
+        const held = LINES.get(lines[i])!;
+        for (const p of held) any.add(p);
+        if (held.size <= GENERIC_PROJECTS) for (const p of held) specific.set(p, (specific.get(p) ?? 0) + 1);
+        if (LICENCE_LINES.has(lines[i])) lic++;
+      }
+      const projects = [...specific].filter(([, k]) => k >= MIN_RUN).map(([p]) => p).sort();
+      const r: Run = { file, from: run[0] + 1, to: run[run.length - 1] + 1, kind: "code", projects: projects.length ? projects : [...any].sort(), lines: run.length };
+      if (lic / run.length >= LICENCE_SHARE) out.licence.push(r);
+      else if (projects.length) out.attributed.push(r);
+      else if (any.size > GENERIC_PROJECTS) out.generic.push(r);
+    }
+    run = [];
+    gap = 0;
+  };
+  lines.forEach((l, i) => {
+    if (!substantive(l)) { if (run.length && ++gap > MAX_GAP) close(); return; }
+    if (LINES.has(l)) { run.push(i); gap = 0; } else close();
+  });
+  close();
+  return out;
+}
+
+/** Prose runs: lines carrying a SHINGLE-word run found in a prose corpus. */
+function proseRuns(file: string, raw: string[]): Run[] {
+  if (!file.endsWith(".md")) return [];
+  const out: Run[] = [];
+  raw.forEach((_, i) => {
+    const w = words(raw.slice(i, i + 4).join(" "));
+    const found = new Set<string>();
+    for (let k = 0; k + SHINGLE <= w.length; k++) {
+      const s = SHINGLES.get(w.slice(k, k + SHINGLE).join(" "));
+      if (s) for (const p of s) found.add(p);
+    }
+    for (const p of found) {
+      const prev = out.findLast((r) => r.projects[0] === p);
+      if (prev && i + 1 <= prev.to + 1) { prev.to = i + 1; prev.lines++; }
+      else out.push({ file, from: i + 1, to: i + 1, kind: "prose", projects: [p], lines: 1 });
+    }
+  });
+  return out;
+}
+
+const all = corpora();
+const notCompared = all.filter((c) => !c.dir);
+for (const c of all) {
+  if (!c.dir) continue;
+  console.error(`${c.name}@${c.version}: ${index(c)} substantive lines`);
+}
+const LICENCE_OF = new Map(all.filter((c) => c.dir).map((c) => [project(c), c.licence]));
+
+const attributed: Run[] = [], licenceRuns: Run[] = [], genericRuns: Run[] = [];
+for (const f of tracked()) {
+  const raw = readFileSync(join(ROOT, f), "utf8").split("\n");
+  const r = codeRuns(f, raw);
+  attributed.push(...r.attributed, ...proseRuns(f, raw));
+  licenceRuns.push(...r.licence);
+  genericRuns.push(...r.generic);
+}
+
+const byProject = new Map<string, Run[]>();
+for (const r of attributed) for (const p of r.projects) {
+  if (!byProject.has(p)) byProject.set(p, []);
+  byProject.get(p)!.push(r);
+}
+const range = (r: Run) => (r.from === r.to ? `${r.from}` : `${r.from}–${r.to}`);
+const table = (runs: Run[], withProjects: boolean) => {
+  const byFile = new Map<string, Run[]>();
+  for (const r of runs) { if (!byFile.has(r.file)) byFile.set(r.file, []); byFile.get(r.file)!.push(r); }
+  let s = withProjects ? "| file | lines | shared by |\n|---|---|---|\n" : "| file | kind | lines |\n|---|---|---|\n";
+  for (const [f, rs] of byFile) {
+    s += withProjects
+      ? `| \`${f}\` | ${rs.map(range).join(", ")} | ${[...new Set(rs.flatMap((r) => r.projects))].length} projects |\n`
+      : `| \`${f}\` | ${[...new Set(rs.map((r) => r.kind))].join(", ")} | ${rs.map(range).join(", ")} |\n`;
+  }
+  return s;
+};
+
+let md = `# Third-party inventory
+
+⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with \`bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts\`.
+
+Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. \`NOTICE\` is
+written from this file. Method: code is **${MIN_RUN} or more substantive lines in a row**,
+with gaps of up to ${MAX_GAP}, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
+is attributed to every project holding ${MIN_RUN} or more of the run's lines; prose is
+**a run of ${SHINGLE} consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
+corpora only. A substantive line has ${MIN_LINE} or more characters and a letter. A run
+is **licence text** when ${LICENCE_SHARE * 100}% of its lines come from licence files, and
+**shared boilerplate** when more than ${GENERIC_PROJECTS} projects hold it; neither is
+attributed, and only lines held by ${GENERIC_PROJECTS} projects or fewer count toward
+attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
+paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
+cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
+which are PDFs under \`docs/references/\` and not in version control;
+\`bitcoin-core/secp256k1\`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
+documentation. \`LICENSE\`, \`NOTICE\` and
+\`LICENSES/\` are not compared.
+
+**${all.length} corpora in ${VERSIONS.size} projects compared; ${byProject.size} projects reproduced; ${notCompared.length} corpora not compared.**
+
+`;
+for (const [p, runs] of [...byProject].sort()) {
+  md += `## ${p} — ${LICENCE_OF.get(p)}\n\nCompared at ${[...VERSIONS.get(p)!].map((v) => `\`${v}\``).join(", ")}.\n\n${table(runs, false)}\n`;
+}
+md += `## Licence text, not attributed\n\n${licenceRuns.length ? table(licenceRuns, true) : "None.\n"}\n`;
+md += `## Shared boilerplate, not attributed\n\n${genericRuns.length ? table(genericRuns, true) : "None.\n"}\n`;
+if (notCompared.length) {
+  md += `## Not compared\n\n${notCompared.map((c) => `- ${c.name} \`${c.version}\`: ${c.licence}`).join("\n")}\n`;
+}
+mkdirSync(join(ROOT, "docs/third-party"), { recursive: true });
+writeFileSync(OUT, md);
+console.log(`wrote ${relative(ROOT, OUT)} — ${byProject.size} projects reproduced, ${licenceRuns.length} licence-text and ${genericRuns.length} boilerplate runs set aside`);
+const found = [...byProject.keys()];
+
+if (process.argv.includes("--check")) {
+  const notice = existsSync(join(ROOT, "NOTICE")) ? readFileSync(join(ROOT, "NOTICE"), "utf8") : "";
+  const missing = found.map((p) => p.replace(/^(crate|npm) /, "")).filter((n) => !notice.includes(n));
+  if (missing.length) {
+    console.log(`check: FAIL — NOTICE does not name: ${missing.join(", ")}`);
+    process.exit(1);
+  }
+  console.log("check: PASS — NOTICE names every project with a hit");
+}

     8	#
     9	# The property: a push that carries the private history goes to the private
    10	# archive and nowhere else. "Carries" means a pushed commit has a recorded root
    11	# as an ancestor. "The archive" means the destination's GitHub repository id
    12	# equals the recorded one and GitHub reports it private. The id survives a
    13	# rename, so the check holds before the rename, after it, and while the new
    14	# public repository is still private, which a visibility check alone would not.
    15	#
    16	# Measured on git 2.50.1 before this was written: git passes the destination
    17	# AFTER `insteadOf`, `pushInsteadOf` and `pushurl` are applied, and runs the
    18	# hook once for every push URL of a remote.
    19	#
    20	# ⚠ A guard against mistakes, not against the owner. `git push --no-verify`
    21	# skips it, and it does nothing in a clone it was never installed in.
    22	#
    23	# `make check-push-guard` breaks it every way it knows and fails if any break
    24	# goes unnoticed.
    25	set -u
    26	
    27	# Prints `owner/name` for a GitHub URL, or fails. Hosts are matched exactly, so
    28	# `github.com.example.org` is not GitHub.
    29	parse_github_url() {
    30	  local u=$1 rest hostpart host path
    31	  case "$u" in
    32	    https://* | http://* | ssh://* | git://*)
    33	      rest=${u#*://}
    34	      hostpart=${rest%%/*}
    35	      [ "$hostpart" = "$rest" ] && return 1
    36	      path=${rest#*/}
    37	      ;;
    38	    *:*)
    39	      # scp-like `[user@]host:path`, which git takes only when no `/` comes
    40	      # before the first `:`.
    41	      hostpart=${u%%:*}
    42	      case "$hostpart" in */*) return 1 ;; esac
    43	      path=${u#*:}
    44	      ;;
    45	    *) return 1 ;;
    46	  esac
    47	  hostpart=${hostpart##*@}
    48	  host=$(printf '%s' "${hostpart%%:*}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    49	  case "$host" in
    50	    github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;
    51	    *) return 1 ;;
    52	  esac
    53	  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
    54	  path=${path%.git}
    55	  while [ "${path%/}" != "$path" ]; do path=${path%/}; done
    56	  case "$path" in
    57	    */*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;
    58	    ?*/?*) ;;
    59	    *) return 1 ;;
    60	  esac
    61	  printf '%s\n' "$path"
    62	}
    63	
    64	if [ "$#" -eq 2 ] && [ "$1" = "--parse-url" ]; then
    65	  parse_github_url "$2"
    66	  exit
    67	fi
    68	
    69	url=${2-}
    70	refuse() {
    71	  printf 'push guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2
    72	  printf '  destination: %s\n' "$url" >&2
    73	  printf '  This history may go only to the private archive. Publish from the\n' >&2
    74	  printf '  export instead: decision request phase 1, item 5, step 4.\n' >&2
    75	  exit 1
    76	}
    77	
    78	roots=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.roots || true)
    79	archive_id=$(git config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid || true)
    80	if [ -z "$roots" ] || [ -z "$archive_id" ]; then
    81	  refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"
    82	fi
    83	for r in $roots; do
    84	  git cat-file -e "${r}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
    85	    || refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"
    86	done
    87	
    88	carries=0
    89	# `|| [ -n … ]` keeps a last line with no newline. git always sends one; the
    90	# guard should not depend on it.
    91	while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do
    92	  [ -n "${local_sha-}" ] || continue
    93	  # A deletion publishes nothing.
    94	  case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    95	  if ! commit=$(git rev-parse -q --verify "${local_sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null); then
    96	    carries=1
    97	    break
    98	  fi
    99	  for r in $roots; do
   100	    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$r" "$commit" 2>/dev/null
   101	    case $? in
   102	      0) carries=1; break 2 ;;
   103	      1) ;;
   104	      *) carries=1; break 2 ;;
   105	    esac
   106	  done
   107	done
   108	[ "$carries" = 0 ] && exit 0
   109	
   110	target=$(parse_github_url "$url") \
   111	  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and the destination is not a GitHub repository"
   112	command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   113	  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and gh is not on PATH, so the destination cannot be checked"
   114	info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private)"' 2>/dev/null) \
   115	  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"
   116	id=${info%% *}
   117	private=${info#* }
   118	[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ] \
   119	  || refuse "this push carries the private history, and $target (repository id $id) is not the archive (id $archive_id)"
   120	[ "$private" = "true" ] \
   121	  || refuse "$target is the archive, but GitHub reports that it is not private"
   122	exit 0
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Installs the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push, in this clone.
     3	#
     4	# Run it in every PRIVATE clone (decision request phase 1, D4 and item 5,
     5	# step 8). It records the archive as the GitHub repository behind the clone's
     6	# own push URL — so run it while `origin` is the private archive, under either
     7	# name — and refuses if GitHub does not report that repository private.
     8	#
     9	# The hook is COPIED, not linked. A link into the tracked file would vanish on
    10	# checking out any commit that predates it, and git treats a missing hook as
    11	# no hook.
    12	#
    13	# Usage: tools/install-push-guard.sh [remote]   (default: origin)
    14	set -euo pipefail
    15	
    16	fail() { printf 'install-push-guard: REFUSED — %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
    17	
    18	top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    19	src="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
    20	[ -f "$src" ] || fail "$src is missing"
    21	
    22	if hooks_path=$(git config --get core.hooksPath); then
    23	  fail "core.hooksPath is set ($hooks_path), so a hook copied into the hooks directory would not run"
    24	fi
    25	hooks_dir=$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)
    26	case "$hooks_dir" in /*) ;; *) hooks_dir="$top/$hooks_dir" ;; esac
    27	dest="$hooks_dir/pre-push"
    28	if [ -e "$dest" ] && ! grep -q '^# wconf push guard' "$dest"; then
    29	  fail "$dest exists and is not this guard; move it aside first"
    30	fi
    31	
    32	remote=${1:-origin}
    33	push_url=$(git remote get-url --push "$remote") || fail "no remote named $remote"
    34	target=$(bash "$src" --parse-url "$push_url") \
    35	  || fail "$remote's push URL is not a GitHub repository: $push_url"
    36	command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "gh is not on PATH"
    37	info=$(gh api "repos/$target" --jq '"\(.id) \(.private) \(.full_name)"') \
    38	  || fail "could not read repos/$target from GitHub"
    39	read -r archive_id private full_name <<<"$info"
    40	[ "$private" = "true" ] || fail "$full_name is not private, so it cannot be the archive"
    41	
    42	roots=$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
    43	roots=${roots% }
    44	[ -n "$roots" ] || fail "this clone has no commits"
    45	
    46	git config wconf.pushguard.archiveid "$archive_id"
    47	git config wconf.pushguard.archivename "$full_name"
    48	git config wconf.pushguard.roots "$roots"
    49	mkdir -p "$hooks_dir"
    50	cp "$src" "$dest"
    51	chmod 0755 "$dest"
    52	
    53	printf 'push guard installed: %s\n' "$dest"
    54	printf '  archive: %s (repository id %s, private)\n' "$full_name" "$archive_id"
    55	printf '  roots:   %s\n' "$roots"
    56	printf '  A push carrying a commit with one of those roots may go only to that\n'
    57	printf '  repository id. It does not run on git push --no-verify, in a clone it\n'
    58	printf '  was never installed in, or if core.hooksPath is set later.\n'
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Self-test for the push guard, tools/git-hooks/pre-push.
     3	#
     4	# Every case runs against the real hook, installed by the real installer into a
     5	# throwaway repository, with a fake `gh` on PATH so nothing touches GitHub.
     6	# Then every case runs again against MUTANTS of the hook, each of which removes
     7	# one protection. A mutant that the cases do not catch fails this check, and so
     8	# does a mutation that does not apply: a case list that a broken hook still
     9	# passes proves nothing.
    10	#
    11	# Needs bash, git and perl. No network.
    12	set -u
    13	
    14	top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    15	HOOK_SRC="$top/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
    16	INSTALL_SRC="$top/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
    17	work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/push-guard.XXXXXX")
    18	trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    19	
    20	G() {
    21	  git -c user.name=guard -c user.email=guard@example.invalid \
    22	      -c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false -c init.defaultBranch=main "$@"
    23	}
    24	ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
    25	FAILED=0
    26	fail() { printf '  ✗ %s\n' "$1"; FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); }
    27	pass() { printf '  ✓ %s\n' "$1"; }
    28	
    29	if hp=$(git config --global --get core.hooksPath); then
    30	  printf 'check-push-guard: FAIL — core.hooksPath is set globally (%s), so the guard cannot run on this machine\n' "$hp"
    31	  exit 1
    32	fi
    33	
    34	# --- a fake gh, answering `gh api repos/<owner>/<name> --jq <expr>` from a table
    35	mkdir -p "$work/bin" "$work/minbin"
    36	cat >"$work/bin/gh" <<'EOF'
    37	#!/usr/bin/env bash
    38	[ "${1-}" = api ] || exit 2
    39	want=$(printf '%s' "${2#repos/}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
    40	while read -r name id private; do
    41	  if [ "$(printf '%s' "$name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" = "$want" ]; then
    42	    case "${4-}" in
    43	      *full_name*) printf '%s %s %s\n' "$id" "$private" "$name" ;;
    44	      *) printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$private" ;;
    45	    esac
    46	    exit 0
    47	  fi
    48	done <"$FAKE_GH_TABLE"
    49	echo 'HTTP 404: Not Found' >&2
    50	exit 1
    51	EOF
    52	chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
    53	for t in bash git tr; do ln -s "$(command -v "$t")" "$work/minbin/$t"; done
    54	PATH_GH="$work/bin:$PATH"
    55	PATH_NO_GH="$work/minbin"
    56	
    57	TABLE="$work/table"
    58	printf 'arch/ive 100 true\npub/lic 200 true\nflip/ped 300 false\n' >"$TABLE"
    59	TABLE_FLIPPED="$work/table-flipped"
    60	printf 'arch/ive 100 false\npub/lic 200 true\n' >"$TABLE_FLIPPED"
    61	
    62	# --- the "private" clone: a history with one root, then the guard installed
    63	P="$work/private"
    64	G init -q "$P"
    65	G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
    66	G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m second
    67	ROOT=$(G -C "$P" rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)
    68	PRIV=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)
    69	mkdir -p "$P/tools/git-hooks"
    70	cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
    71	cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$P/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
    72	G -C "$P" remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git
    73	
    74	echo "The installer:"
    75	if out=$(cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1); then
    76	  pass "installs against a private archive"
    77	else
    78	  fail "installs against a private archive: $out"
    79	fi
    80	[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.archiveid)" = 100 ] \
    81	  && pass "records the archive's repository id" || fail "records the archive's repository id"
    82	[ "$(G -C "$P" config --get wconf.pushguard.roots)" = "$ROOT" ] \
    83	  && pass "records the history's root" || fail "records the history's root"
    84	cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push" \
    85	  && pass "copies the hook byte for byte" || fail "copies the hook byte for byte"
    86	
    87	installer_refuses() { # <label> <needle> <setup...>
    88	  local label=$1 needle=$2 d="$work/inst.$RANDOM"
    89	  shift 2
    90	  G init -q "$d" && G -C "$d" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
    91	  mkdir -p "$d/tools/git-hooks"
    92	  cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$d/tools/git-hooks/pre-push"
    93	  cp "$INSTALL_SRC" "$d/tools/install-push-guard.sh"
    94	  (cd "$d" && "$@")
    95	  local o rc
    96	  o=$(cd "$d" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" bash tools/install-push-guard.sh 2>&1)
    97	  rc=$?
    98	  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "$o" | grep -qF "$needle"; then pass "$label"; else fail "$label (exit $rc): $o"; fi
    99	}
   100	installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not private" "is not private" \
   101	  git remote add origin https://github.com/flip/ped.git
   102	installer_refuses "refuses when core.hooksPath is set" "core.hooksPath is set" \
   103	  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && git config core.hooksPath .hooks'
   104	installer_refuses "refuses to overwrite a foreign pre-push hook" "is not this guard" \
   105	  sh -c 'git remote add origin https://github.com/arch/ive.git && printf "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n" > .git/hooks/pre-push'
   106	installer_refuses "refuses an origin that is not on GitHub" "not a GitHub repository" \
   107	  git remote add origin "$work/somewhere.git"
   108	
   109	# History created AFTER the install, as it would be in the real clone.
   110	G -C "$P" tag -a -m t ptag "$PRIV"
   111	TAGOBJ=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse ptag)
   112	G -C "$P" checkout -q --orphan clean
   113	G -C "$P" commit -q --allow-empty -m orphan
   114	ORPH=$(G -C "$P" rev-parse HEAD)
   115	G -C "$P" checkout -q main
   116	
   117	# A clone with the hook but no configuration, and one whose recorded root is absent.
   118	U="$work/unconfigured"
   119	G init -q "$U" && G -C "$U" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
   120	cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$U/.git/hooks/pre-push"
   121	S="$work/shallow"
   122	G init -q "$S" && G -C "$S" commit -q --allow-empty -m root
   123	cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$S/.git/hooks/pre-push"
   124	G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.archiveid 100
   125	G -C "$S" config wconf.pushguard.roots 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
   126	
   127	ref() { printf 'refs/heads/main %s refs/heads/main %s\n' "$1" "$ZERO"; }
   128	
   129	# One case: <name> <0|1> <needle or -> <url> <stdin> [repo] [PATH] [table]
   130	case_result() {
   131	  local name=$1 want=$2 needle=$3 url=$4 input=$5 repo=${6:-$P} path=${7:-$PATH_GH} table=${8:-$TABLE}
   132	  local out rc
   133	  out=$(cd "$repo" && printf '%s' "$input" | PATH="$path" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$table" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push" origin "$url" 2>&1)
   134	  rc=$?
   135	  if [ "$want" = 0 ]; then
   136	    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]
   137	  else
   138	    [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && { [ "$needle" = - ] || printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF "$needle"; }
   139	  fi
   140	}
   141	
   142	NOT_ARCHIVE="is not the archive"
   143	NOT_GITHUB="is not a GitHub repository"
   144	CASES=(
   145	  "A1|0|-|https://github.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
   146	  "A2|0|-|git@github.com:arch/ive.git|PRIV"
   147	  "A3|0|-|https://GITHUB.COM/Arch/Ive.git/|PRIV"
   148	  "A4|0|-|ssh://ssh.github.com:443/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
   149	  "R1|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV"
   150	  "R2|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|git@github.com:pub/lic.git|PRIV"
   151	  "R3|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|ssh://git@github.com/pub/lic|PRIV"
   152	  "R4|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/PUB/LIC.git/|PRIV"
   153	  "R5|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://git@github.com/pub/lic|PRIV"
   154	  "R6|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic//|PRIV"
   155	  "R7|1|$NOT_GITHUB|$work/public.git|PRIV"
   156	  "R8|1|$NOT_GITHUB|file://$work/public.git|PRIV"
   157	  "R9|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com.example.org/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
   158	  "R10|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://example.org/github.com/arch/ive|PRIV"
   159	  "R11|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://gitlab.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV"
   160	  "R12|1|$NOT_GITHUB|https://github.com/arch/ive/extra|PRIV"
   161	  "R13|1|could not be read|https://github.com/no/such|PRIV"
   162	  "R14|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|TAG"
   163	  "R15|1|$NOT_ARCHIVE|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|MIXED"
   164	  "R16|1|gh is not on PATH|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|NOGH"
   165	  "R17|1|is not private|https://github.com/arch/ive.git|PRIV|FLIPPED"
   166	  "R18|1|not configured|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|UNCONF"
   167	  "R19|1|is not in this clone|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|PRIV|SHALLOW"
   168	  "O1|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|ORPH"
   169	  "O2|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|DELETE"
   170	  "O3|0|-|https://github.com/pub/lic.git|EMPTY"
   171	)
   172	CASE_COUNT=${#CASES[@]}
   173	
   174	# Runs every case; prints the names that fail, one per line.
   175	run_cases() {
   176	  local c name want needle url what mode input repo path table
   177	  for c in "${CASES[@]}"; do
   178	    IFS='|' read -r name want needle url what mode <<<"$c"
   179	    repo=$P path=$PATH_GH table=$TABLE
   180	    case "$what" in
   181	      PRIV) input=$(ref "$PRIV") ;;
   182	      TAG) input=$(printf 'refs/tags/ptag %s refs/tags/ptag %s\n' "$TAGOBJ" "$ZERO") ;;
   183	      MIXED) input=$(ref "$ORPH"; printf 'refs/heads/two %s refs/heads/two %s\n' "$PRIV" "$ZERO") ;;
   184	      ORPH) input=$(ref "$ORPH") ;;
   185	      DELETE) input=$(printf '(delete) %s refs/heads/old %s\n' "$ZERO" "$PRIV") ;;
   186	      EMPTY) input= ;;
   187	    esac
   188	    case "${mode-}" in
   189	      NOGH) path=$PATH_NO_GH ;;
   190	      FLIPPED) table=$TABLE_FLIPPED ;;
   191	      UNCONF) repo=$U ;;
   192	      SHALLOW) repo=$S ;;
   193	    esac
   194	    case_result "$name" "$want" "$needle" "$url" "$input" "$repo" "$path" "$table" || echo "$name"
   195	  done
   196	}
   197	
   198	echo
   199	echo "The hook, ${CASE_COUNT} cases:"
   200	failed_cases=$(run_cases)
   201	if [ -z "$failed_cases" ]; then
   202	  pass "all ${CASE_COUNT} cases"
   203	else
   204	  for n in $failed_cases; do fail "case $n"; done
   205	fi
   206	
   207	echo
   208	echo "Through git itself:"
   209	G init -q --bare "$work/public.git"
   210	if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
   211	  fail "a real push of the private history is refused"
   212	else
   213	  G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/main >/dev/null \
   214	    && fail "a real push of the private history is refused (but the ref arrived)" \
   215	    || pass "a real push of the private history is refused, and nothing arrives"
   216	fi
   217	if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q "$work/public.git" clean 2>/dev/null) \
   218	   && [ "$(G -C "$work/public.git" rev-parse refs/heads/clean)" = "$ORPH" ]; then
   219	  pass "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
   220	else
   221	  fail "a real push of a commit without the private history goes through"
   222	fi
   223	if (cd "$P" && PATH="$PATH_GH" FAKE_GH_TABLE="$TABLE" G push -q --dry-run "$work/public.git" main 2>/dev/null); then
   224	  fail "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
   225	else
   226	  pass "a dry run is refused too, so the guard can be proved against a real repository safely"
   227	fi
   228	
   229	# --- mutants: each removes one protection, and the named case must catch it
   230	echo
   231	echo "Mutants — each must be caught by the case named:"
   232	# Four parallel arrays, because several patterns contain `|`.
   233	M_MUST=() M_LABEL=() M_FROM=() M_TO=()
   234	mutant() { M_MUST+=("$1"); M_LABEL+=("$2"); M_FROM+=("$3"); M_TO+=("$4"); }
   235	mutant R1 "ancestry not detected" '0) carries=1; break 2 ;;' '0) ;;'
   236	mutant R1 "every ref skipped" 'case "$local_sha" in *[!0]*) ;; *) continue ;; esac' 'continue'
   237	mutant R1 "repository id not compared" '[ "$id" = "$archive_id" ]' 'true'
   238	mutant R9 "host matched loosely" 'github.com | www.github.com | ssh.github.com) ;;' '*github.com*) ;;'
   239	mutant R12 "extra path segments accepted" "*/*/* | /* | */ | '') return 1 ;;" "/* | */ | '') return 1 ;;"
   240	mutant R13 "fail-open when GitHub cannot be read" '|| refuse "this push carries the private history, and repos/$target could not be read from GitHub"' '|| exit 0'
   241	mutant R15 "only the first pushed ref read" 'while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' 'read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; for _once in 1; do'
   242	mutant R1 "a last line with no newline dropped" ' || [ -n "${local_ref-}" ]; do' '; do'
   243	mutant R17 "archive's visibility not checked" '[ "$private" = "true" ]' 'true'
   244	mutant R18 "unconfigured clone allowed" 'refuse "the guard is not configured in this clone; run make install-push-guard"' 'exit 0'
   245	mutant R19 "absent root not refused" '|| refuse "recorded root $r is not in this clone (a shallow clone?), so nothing can be checked"' '|| true'
   246	MUTANT_COUNT=${#M_MUST[@]}
   247	# A mutant counts as caught only if its case passed on the real hook. If the real
   248	# hook fails any case, every mutant would look caught, so none is evaluated.
   249	if [ -n "$failed_cases" ]; then
   250	  fail "no mutant evaluated: the real hook fails cases, so a mutant's failures would prove nothing"
   251	  M_MUST=()
   252	fi
   253	for i in "${!M_MUST[@]}"; do
   254	  must=${M_MUST[$i]} label=${M_LABEL[$i]}
   255	  for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do
   256	    cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
   257	    FROM=${M_FROM[$i]} TO=${M_TO[$i]} perl -0pi -e 's/\Q$ENV{FROM}\E/$ENV{TO}/' "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"
   258	  done
   259	  if cmp -s "$HOOK_SRC" "$P/.git/hooks/pre-push"; then
   260	    fail "mutant '$label' did not apply — the pattern no longer matches the hook"
   261	    continue
   262	  fi
   263	  caught=$(run_cases)
   264	  if printf '%s\n' "$caught" | grep -qx "$must"; then
   265	    pass "'$label' is caught by $must"
   266	  else
   267	    fail "'$label' is NOT caught by $must (cases failing: $(printf '%s' "$caught" | tr '\n' ' '))"
   268	  fi
   269	done
   270	for repo in "$P" "$U" "$S"; do cp "$HOOK_SRC" "$repo/.git/hooks/pre-push"; done
   271	
   272	echo
   273	echo "What this does not check:"
   274	echo "  1. git push --no-verify, which skips every hook; a clone the guard was never"
   275	echo "     installed in; and core.hooksPath set after the install."
   276	echo "  2. Real GitHub. gh is faked here. make install-push-guard reads the real"
   277	echo "     archive, and a git push --dry-run to a real public repository proves the"
   278	echo "     refusal without sending anything."
   279	echo "  3. The hook treats a merge-base error as carrying the private history. No case"
   280	echo "     produces that error, so that branch has no mutant."
   281	echo
   282	if [ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]; then
   283	  printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=PASS cases=%d mutants=%d exit=0\n' "$CASE_COUNT" "$MUTANT_COUNT"
   284	  exit 0
   285	fi
   286	printf 'check-push-guard: verdict=FAIL failures=%d exit=1\n' "$FAILED"
   287	exit 1

# Third-party inventory

⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with `bun run tools/inventory-third-party.ts`.

Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. `NOTICE` is
written from this file. Method: code is **4 or more substantive lines in a row**,
with gaps of up to 2, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
is attributed to every project holding 4 or more of the run's lines; prose is
**a run of 12 consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
corpora only. A substantive line has 20 or more characters and a letter. A run
is **licence text** when 80% of its lines come from licence files, and
**shared boilerplate** when more than 3 projects hold it; neither is
attributed, and only lines held by 3 projects or fewer count toward
attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
which are PDFs under `docs/references/` and not in version control;
`bitcoin-core/secp256k1`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
documentation. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and
`LICENSES/` are not compared.

**108 corpora in 91 projects compared; 6 projects reproduced; 14 corpora not compared.**

docs/reviews/REVIEW-006-tools-2026-08-17.md:25:  The first hash path matches the documented 51-byte layout, and zero/out-of-range scalars are rejected. The problem is the retry path: this code rehashes only the 32-byte digest (`r = sha256(r)`), while upstream `generate_canonical_encrypted_zero` copies the 32-byte digest into the first 32 bytes of the 51-byte buffer and hashes all 51 bytes again. That branch is rare for secp256k1, but this is consensus-relevant deterministic encoding; if any public input lands on an invalid first scalar, this harness will compute a different EncZero than validators and can falsely fail F-1. The live-ledger positive check and perturbed-account control do not exercise this branch, so E-59 overstates the cross-check coverage.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-006-tools-2026-08-17.md:48:- **Rejection sampling & termination**: `isValidScalar` strictly enforces $0 < n < \text{CURVE.n}$. With secp256k1 order $n \approx 2^{256} - 2^{128}$, rejection probability is $\approx 2^{-128}$, ensuring termination in 1 iteration with overwhelming probability.

docs/reviews/REVIEW-010-RULING-r-and-rho-2026-08-18.md:7:**Verdict: structured fresh randomness.** `r` and `rho` are generated by the signer from 64 bytes of fresh CSPRNG entropy per transaction attempt, then domain-framed with the transaction context and reduced as wide secp256k1 scalars. docs/reviews/REVIEW-010-RULING-r-and-rho-2026-08-18.md:40:**Wide 64-byte reduction carries over.** Each scalar is the integer value of a 64-byte HMAC-SHA-512 block reduced modulo the secp256k1 group order. The reason transfers: reduction from 512 bits gives a negligible-bias scalar without a secret-dependent retry branch.

docs/reviews/REVIEW-024b-codex-ed25519-nonce-2026-08-27.md:189:The proposed combiner is reasoned rather than standardized or supplied by `ed25519-dalek`. Its benefit is also narrow. The losing issue #1 argument remains strong: a same-host adversary with enough control to inject faults into signing may be able to read the signing key directly from process memory, making nonce hedging irrelevant. Pure RFC 8032 avoids dependence on runtime entropy, retains independent byte-for-byte vectors on the live path, and has substantially less maintenance surface. Option C—requiring secp256k1 accounts—would avoid new signature-scheme code entirely.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-024b-codex-ed25519-nonce-2026-08-27.md:223:The judgement call is whether the narrow fault-resistance benefit justifies enabling `hazmat` and maintaining a project-specific nonce-prefix combiner, rather than accepting deterministic RFC 8032 as a named gap or requiring secp256k1 accounts. The equation, exact fallback, and same-implementation vector arm are relatively clear; the benefit-versus-new-cryptographic-surface decision is where a reasonable reviewer could rule the other way.

docs/reviews/REVIEW-005b-ruling-cryptography-leg-B-2026-08-17.md:55:1. **The paper's Remark 6.1, read literally, is broken in its deterministic mode.** `cmpt-compact-sigma.pdf` §6.1 derives nonces over `sk_A ‖ r ‖ m ‖ b ‖ ρ ‖ statement ‖ fresh entropy`. Under the paper's own terminology (§2.4, §6.2) the *statement* `x` **does not include `TransactionContextID`** — §6.2 lists it as a separate, fourth hash input. But the challenge `e` **does** include it. Two proofs with identical statements and different `TransactionContextID`s therefore get **identical nonces under distinct challenges**, which is exactly the extraction condition of Theorem 4.2. This is reachable: a wallet that caches ciphertexts and commitments and re-proves after the on-ledger `CB_S_Version` advances — the routine case created by TOB-RIPCTX-12 and the still-**Unresolved** TOB-RIPCTX-13 — produces precisely that pair. The paper's optional "fresh entropy" is what papers over this. Bind the context properly and the hedging becomes unnecessary; leave it unbound and hedging is the only thing standing between you and `sk_A`. ADR §(e) line 180 copies the gap verbatim.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# ci.sh — everything that runs WITHOUT the vendored build, in one list.
#
#   tools/ci.sh        # or: make ci
#
# GitHub Actions runs exactly this script (.github/workflows/ci.yml), and the
# README's five-minute path tells a stranger to run it too. One list, so the
# workflow, the README and CONTRIBUTING.md cannot drift apart on what is covered.
#
# ⚠ **What this does NOT run, and why** — printed at the end of every run too:
#
# * `cargo test` in `signer/`, `make check-test-support`, `make check-zeroize-bounds`
#   and `make break-zeroize-lock`. All four compile the signer, which links a
#   patched, vendored `mpt-crypto` that `tools/rebuild-env.sh` builds from pinned
#   clones with Homebrew `openssl@3`. That is a macOS build this workflow does not
#   perform.
# * Five facility tests that start a real signer. They are SKIPPED by name, not
#   passed: this script sets `WCONF_SKIP_SIGNER_TESTS=1`, and Bun reports them as
#   `skip`.
# * The known-value half of the secret sweep. `check-no-secrets-shapes` runs the
#   shape classes only; the full `make check-no-secrets` needs the local secret
#   store and runs on the owner's machine. Its verdict word says which it was.
# * `check-filing` on the historical drafts. It runs on the template, as a positive
#   control; 15 of the 20 committed drafts predate the rules it enforces.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

FAILED=()
step() {
  printf '\n=== %s\n' "$*"
  if "$@"; then echo "--- ok: $*"; else echo "--- FAILED: $*"; FAILED+=("$*"); fi
}

step bunx tsc --noEmit
step env WCONF_SKIP_SIGNER_TESTS=1 bun test facility web/api tools
for gate in check-tables check-negative-claims check-personas check-blinding \
            check-loopback check-web-readonly check-disclosure-phrases \
            check-claims-index check-claims-topics check-claims-revisions \
            check-emphasis check-vocabulary check-no-secrets-shapes \
            check-push-guard; do
  step make "$gate"
done
step make check-filing FILE=docs/upstream-filings/TEMPLATE.md

cat <<'EOF'

=== NOT RUN by this script (see its header): cargo test, check-test-support,
    check-zeroize-bounds and break-zeroize-lock, which need the vendored build;
    five facility tests that start a real signer, reported as skip; the
    known-value half of the secret sweep, which needs the local store; and
    check-filing on the historical drafts.
EOF

if [ "${#FAILED[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  printf '\nci: FAILED %d step(s):\n' "${#FAILED[@]}"
  printf '  %s\n' "${FAILED[@]}"
  exit 1
fi
echo
echo "ci: every step passed"

What this gate does NOT catch (each is an asserted-uncaught control):
  - a secret split across two string literals or two lines
  - a secret in UTF-16, base64, gzip or any other re-encoding
  - an unlabelled 64-hex ElGamal secret that is NOT in the local store (no shape rule can tell it from a hash)
  - a seed or key in RFC 1751 words, or as a decimal or byte array
  - a home path under a user name on the generic list
  - a labelled scalar printed in fewer than 48 hex digits: a uniform key is that short with probability below 2^-64
  - a secret listed as an array element under a label, rather than as the value of a key
  - gitignored files, the reflog and unreachable objects: none of them is published
  - a hostname, a machine serial, or a person's name — only paths and email addresses are personal-data classes

Which tracked files reproduce upstream source or specification text. `NOTICE` is
written from this file. Method: code is **4 or more substantive lines in a row**,
with gaps of up to 2, each verbatim in a corpus after collapsing whitespace, and
is attributed to every project holding 4 or more of the run's lines; prose is
**a run of 12 consecutive words**, searched in the specification and documentation
corpora only. A substantive line has 20 or more characters and a letter. A run
is **licence text** when 80% of its lines come from licence files, and
**shared boilerplate** when more than 3 projects hold it; neither is
attributed, and only lines held by 3 projects or fewer count toward
attribution. ⚠ **What this cannot see**: a quotation shorter than those thresholds, a
paraphrase, and a source that is not a corpus below. Sources the records are known to
cite and that are **not** corpora: the Trail of Bits report and the Dore and Cenk papers,
which are PDFs under `docs/references/` and not in version control;
`bitcoin-core/secp256k1`; and web pages quoted a sentence at a time, such as GitHub's
documentation. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and
`LICENSES/` are not compared.

docs/reviews/REVIEW-005b-ruling-cryptography-leg-B-2026-08-17.md:476:- **The Clawback transcript's `PT(m·G)` for `m = 0`.** `0·G` is the point at infinity, which libsecp256k1 cannot serialise — the same defect class as TOB-RIPCTX-5 and TOB-RIPCTX-6. docs/reviews/REVIEW-012c-adjudication-keygen-2026-08-18.md:35:Leg B shipped two known-answer vectors, computed by executing code. docs/reviews/REVIEW-012b-codex-keygen-2026-08-18.md:31:4. **Seed input:** feed the decoded XRPL family seed entropy, not a derived XRPL private key. `ripple-address-codec` encodes seeds from exactly 16 entropy bytes plus a seed type (`node_modules/ripple-address-codec/src/xrp-codec.ts:165`, `node_modules/ripple-address-codec/src/xrp-codec.ts:178`), and decodes to `bytes` plus `type` (`node_modules/ripple-address-codec/src/xrp-codec.ts:185`, `node_modules/ripple-address-codec/src/xrp-codec.ts:201`). For regular-key or multi-signing accounts, this profile may be used only with the AccountRoot master family seed for the account being registered; a regular-key seed or a signer-list member seed must be refused as the derivation root.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-012b-codex-keygen-2026-08-18.md:39:8. **Standard or repository-local:** repository-local now, with public vectors and a stable spec. docs/reviews/REVIEW-055-packets/f12-round-two-transcript.txt:1653:`secp256k1_bulletproof_prove_agg` documents `*proof_len` as the caller's buffer capacity on input, but overwrites it with `proof_size` immediately after validating `m`. The only capacity check, in the serialization block, then compares that value against a locally recomputed `expected` equal to it, so `*proof_len < expected` is dead for every supported `m`, and an undersized `proof_out` is serialized past its end.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-055-packets/f12-round-two-transcript.txt:1663:`secp256k1_bulletproof_create_commitment` dereferenced `h_generator` and `commitment_C` without validating them, so a NULL required pointer crashed the process instead of returning the documented 0 (confirmed: SIGSEGV on unpatched `main`). Added `MPT_ARG_CHECK` entry-point checks, the idiom already used across `elgamal.c` and the proof modules. The same checks are added to `prove_agg`, which had the identical gap the scan did not flag. `context_id` is deliberately excluded: it is documented optional and NULL-guarded at every transcript absorption.
docs/reviews/REVIEW-055-packets/f12-round-two-transcript.txt:1667:`secp256k1_elgamal_add` / `_subtract` cannot represent an identity result, because a `secp256k1_pubkey` has no encoding for the point at infinity; subtracting a ciphertext from itself, or any pair sharing a component, returns 0 indistinguishably from a genuine failure. Giving the ciphertext an identity-capable representation changes the exported representation downstream consumers build on, so this PR documents the limitation in the API contract and pins it with tests instead. Whether to change the representation is a protocol decision, not a library one, and it is the same underlying mechanism as AXRT-4218 at the transactor layer, so the two are worth deciding together. Both functions are WASM-exported specifically for client-side chained-balance prediction (`CB_S' = CB_S -/+ the encrypted amount`), which is the path that can actually reach a cancellation, so the header now points callers at `generate_canonical_encrypted_zero()` for a zero balance.

docs/reviews/REVIEW-051-packets/packet-a-filing-prep.md:81:| F-19 | **mpt-crypto's exported PoK API makes account binding optional, and the public header does not say so.** `secp256k1_mpt_pok_sk_verify(ctx, proof, pk, context_id)` accepts a NULL `context_id` — `/* context_id is optional */` in `proof_pok_sk.c`, and `build_pok_challenge` folds the context in only `if (context_id)`. With NULL, the challenge is `SHA-256("CMPT_POK_SK_REGISTER" ‖ pk ‖ T)`: a valid registration proof bound to **nothing but the public key**, and therefore **replayable by any party who has seen it, on any account, on any chain**. The **public header** `include/secp256k1_mpt.h:219–224` declares both `_prove` and `_verify` with the parameter and ~~**no doc comment whatsoever**~~ no doc comment that mentions `context_id` (E-296) — the optionality and its cost are visible only by reading the `.c`. ⚠ **This does NOT affect the ledger.** rippled cannot reach the NULL path: the utility wrapper `mpt_verify_convert_proof` rejects a NULL context hash before forwarding (E-66), and rippled always supplies a `uint256`. **Never describe this as an XLS-96 vulnerability.** The exposure is to *other* consumers of the exported library — a Rust or WASM binding, or this project's own signer harness — for whom passing NULL compiles, runs, verifies, and silently produces a forgeable registration | **Read at source 2026-08-18** at `85dbac7` = `1.0.4`: `proof_pok_sk.c` (`build_pok_challenge`, both `MPT_ARG_CHECK` blocks), `include/secp256k1_mpt.h:211–224`, `src/utility/mpt_utility.cpp:864`. Found while closing issue #4. → `UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md` U-38. **Not filed** — nothing is filed without first checking the April Trail of Bits report and its fix-review appendix. Checked 2026-09-14: the report raises this in Appendices B and D, its fix review does not track either, and upstream has documented the field as optional on one function but not made it required (E-296). On the failing path, the caller sees a\nhalf-populated output buffer and a failure return code — easy to\nmisuse, and harder to audit than a strict \"compute everything in\ntemporaries, then commit\" pattern.\n\n## Specific sites (line numbers from TOB May 2026; verify by\nfunction name during sweep)\n\n**`mpt-crypto` utility wrappers (`src/utility/mpt_utility.cpp`):**\n\n- `mpt_get_confidential_send_proof` (~L554): calls\n  `secp256k1_compact_standard_prove` (which can `return -1`) before\n  the `amount > balance_params->amount` check, and before the\n  bulletproof generation at `mpt_get_bulletproof_agg` which can\n  fail and `return rc`. A failing path can leave the compact-proof\n  prefix written to `out_proof`.\n- `mpt_get_convert_back_proof` (~L689): writes the compact\n  ConvertBack proof to `out_proof` before computing the BP and\n  appending it. If the shared-secret multiplication returns 0\n  or the later point combination returns 0, `c1` is already\n  modified.\n- `secp256k1_elgamal_add` (~L183): writes `sum_c1` before\n  computing `sum_c2`. If the second combine fails, the function\n  returns 0 with `sum_c1` already modified.\n- `secp256k1_elgamal_subtract` (~L213): same pattern with\n  `diff_c1`.\n\n## Recommended pattern\n\nCompute all derived outputs in local temporaries first, perform all\nchecks, and **only then** copy into caller-provided buffers. Where\nthat is infeasible, document at the API boundary that partial\noutput may exist on failure and require the caller to treat the\nbuffer as undefined.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Each site listed above either uses the temporary-then-copy\n  pattern, or its public doxygen explicitly documents that the\n  output buffer may be partially written on failure.\n- Negative tests cover the partial-write path: deliberately\n  trigger the inner failure and assert that either (a) the output\n  buffer is unchanged from its pre-call state, or (b) the\n  function's documented behavior is honored.\n\n## References\n\n- TOB May 2026 Appendix E, pp. 66-68 (mpt-crypto + elgamal\n  subsection). docs/reviews/REVIEW-055-packets/f12-round-one-transcript.txt:1247:{"baseRefName":"main","body":"### Why\n`mpt-crypto` is used by XRPL client SDKs/libraries in two ways: native shared libraries (xrpl4j, xrpl-py) and a WebAssembly module (xrpl.js). PR #56 gave the **native** libraries a full CI story — build per platform, run `ctest`, bundle, and attach to the GitHub release. The **WASM** module had no equivalent: no CI build, no tests, and no released artifact.\n\nThis PR brings WASM to parity, so JS/TS consumers can pull a reproducibly-built, tested wasm module from tagged releases — the same guarantee xrpl4j/xrpl-py already get for the native libs.\n\n## What it adds\n```\nbuild-wasm.yml  (one ubuntu job, called by build.yml)\n   │\n   ├─ setup emsdk 6.0.2 + Node 22\n   ├─ build-wasm.sh   → compiles secp256k1 + OpenSSL + mpt-crypto, then links the\n   │                    glue TWICE → emcc_out/mpt_crypto.{js, mjs, wasm}\n   │                      • mpt_crypto.js   MODULARIZE CommonJS glue\n   │                      • mpt_crypto.mjs  EXPORT_ES6 ES-module glue\n   │                      • mpt_crypto.wasm the single shared module both glues wrap\n   ├─ test-wasm.sh    → (1) compiles the crypto test suite to wasm, runs it under\n   │                    Node via ctest; (2) smoke-tests BOTH shipped glues     ← gate\n   └─ bundle + upload → mpt-crypto-wasm-bundle  (js + mjs + wasm)\n                                        │\n   build.yml `release` job (on tag) ────┘\n        needs [build-and-test, native-binaries, wasm]\n        → attaches mpt-crypto-wasm-<tag>.tar.gz to the GitHub release (next to the native bundle)\n```\n\nWASM is a single portable target, so there's no OS×arch matrix — one wasm32 module runs in every browser and in Node/Deno on any platform.\n\n## Dual glue: one wasm, CommonJS + ES module\nThe wasm module is consumed by xrpl.js, which ships as a **dual CJS+ESM package**. To serve both without shipping the wasm twice, `build-wasm.sh` links the glue **twice from the identical object files**, both wrapping the **same** `mpt_crypto.wasm`:\n\n| Output | emcc flags | Consumer |\n|---|---|---|\n| `mpt_crypto.js` | `MODULARIZE` (CommonJS) | Node / Jest (`require`) — reads the `.wasm` off disk |\n| `mpt_crypto.mjs` | `-sEXPORT_ES6=1` (ES module) | bundlers / browsers (`import`) — locates the wasm via `new URL('mpt_crypto.wasm', import.meta.url)`, which webpack/rollup turn into an emitted asset |\n\nThe ESM glue is what lets Confidential MPT run in the browser: the CommonJS glue statically `require`s `node:fs`/`node:crypto` and can't be bundled, whereas the `new URL(import.meta.url)` form makes bundlers emit the wasm as a fetchable asset. Both glues are byte-for-byte the same ABI over the same module — shipping the trio together keeps the glue and wasm in lockstep.\n\n## File by file\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `.github/scripts/build-wasm.sh` | **Builds the module.** `emcc` link that statically bundles secp256k1 + a stripped OpenSSL, then emits **both** glues (`mpt_crypto.js` MODULARIZE + `mpt_crypto.mjs` EXPORT_ES6) over the same `mpt_crypto.wasm`. Reads dep versions from `conan.lock`; verifies dependency integrity (pinned secp256k1 commit + OpenSSL tarball SHA-256); forces static secp256k1 (`-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`); exports only the symbols consumers use. |\n| `.github/scripts/test-wasm.sh` | **Validates it.** (1) Compiles the C crypto test suite to wasm32 and runs each test under Node via `ctest`, reusing the deps `build-wasm.sh` just built. (2) Smoke-tests **both shipped glues** the way consumers load them (`require` the `.js`, `import` the `.mjs`): instantiate, init the secp256k1 context, then `malloc` + run one export + read `HEAPU8` — so a bad `-s` flag or ABI break fails here, not downstream. |\n| `.github/workflows/build-wasm.yml` | **The CI workflow.** Reusable (`workflow_call`), single ubuntu job, no matrix. Runs the two scripts, bundles the output (js + mjs + wasm), uploads `mpt-crypto-wasm-bundle`. |\n| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | **Wires it in.** Adds a `wasm` job beside `native-binaries`, adds it to `release.needs`, and attaches the wasm tarball on tag push. |\n| `.gitignore` | Ignores the emscripten build outputs (`emcc_build/`, `emcc_out/`). |\n\n## Dependency integrity\nThe native build gets integrity from Conan (`conan.lock` revisions + source SHA-256). This WASM path fetches secp256k1 (git tag) and OpenSSL (release tarball) directly, so it verifies them explicitly to match that guarantee:\n- **secp256k1** — the checked-out commit is verified against a pinned SHA (a git tag is mutable; the commit is not).\n- **OpenSSL** — the tarball's SHA-256 is verified against a pinned hash before extraction.\n\n## How it's tested\n`test-wasm.sh` runs two layers, both gating the `release` job:\n1. **Crypto** — compiles mpt-crypto's C crypto test suite to wasm32 and runs all 11 tests under Node via `ctest`.\n2. **Glue / ABI** — loads each shipped glue the consumer way (`require` the `.js`, `import` the `.mjs`) and exercises the marshalling contract end to end (secp256k1 context init + `malloc` / `mpt_generate_blinding_factor` / `HEAPU8`).\n\nSo a wasm build whose crypto misbehaves — or whose glue/ABI a bad emcc flag has broken — can't ship.\n","comments":[],"commits":[{"authoredDate":"2026-07-20T16:51:45Z","authors":[{"email":"redacted@example.invalid","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjEzNTE0OTMz","login":"kuan121","name":"Kuan /**
 * Utils for modular division and fields.
 * Field over 11 is a finite (Galois) field is integer number operations `mod 11`.
 * There is no division: it is replaced by modular multiplicative inverse.
 * @module
 */
/*! noble-curves - MIT License (c) 2022 Paul Miller (paulmillr.com) */
import {
  _validateObject,
  anumber,
  bitMask,
  bytesToNumberBE,
  bytesToNumberLE,
  ensureBytes,
  numberToBytesBE,
  numberToBytesLE,
} from '../utils.ts';

// prettier-ignore
const _0n = BigInt(0), _1n = BigInt(1), _2n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(2), _3n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(3);
// prettier-ignore
const _4n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(4), _5n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(5), _7n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(7);
// prettier-ignore
const _8n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(8), _9n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(9), _16n = /* @__PURE__ */ BigInt(16);

// Calculates a modulo b
export function mod(a: bigint, b: bigint): bigint {
  const result = a % b;
  return result >= _0n ? result : b + result;
}
/**
 * Efficiently raise num to power and do modular division.
 * Unsafe in some contexts: uses ladder, so can expose bigint bits.
 * @example
 * pow(2n, 6n, 11n) // 64n % 11n == 9n
 */
export function pow(num: bigint, power: bigint, modulo: bigint): bigint {
  return FpPow(Field(modulo), num, power);
}

/** Does `x^(2^power)` mod p. `pow2(30, 4)` == `30^(2^4)` */
export function pow2(x: bigint, power: bigint, modulo: bigint): bigint {
  let res = x;
  while (power-- > _0n) {
    res *= res;
    res %= modulo;
  }
  return res;
}

/**
 * Inverses number over modulo.
 * Implemented using [Euclidean GCD](https://brilliant.org/wiki/extended-euclidean-algorithm/).
 */
export function invert(number: bigint, modulo: bigint): bigint {
  if (number === _0n) throw new Error('invert: expected non-zero number');
  if (modulo <= _0n) throw new Error('invert: expected positive modulus, got ' + modulo);
  // Fermat's little theorem "CT-like" version inv(n) = n^(m-2) mod m is 30x slower.
  let a = mod(number, modulo);
  let b = modulo;
  // prettier-ignore
  let x = _0n, y = _1n, u = _1n, v = _0n;
  while (a !== _0n) {
    // JIT applies optimization if those two lines follow each other
    const q = b / a;
    const r = b % a;
    const m = x - u * q;
    const n = y - v * q;
    // prettier-ignore
    b = a, a = r, x = u, y = v, u = m, v = n;
  }
  const gcd = b;
  if (gcd !== _1n) throw new Error('invert: does not exist');
  return mod(x, modulo);
}

function assertIsSquare<T>(Fp: IField<T>, root: T, n: T): void {
  if (!Fp.eql(Fp.sqr(root), n)) throw new Error('Cannot find square root');
}

// Not all roots are possible! Example which will throw:
// const NUM =
// n = 72057594037927816n;
// Fp = Field(BigInt('0x1a0111ea397fe69a4b1ba7b6434bacd764774b84f38512bf6730d2a0f6b0f6241eabfffeb153ffffb9feffffffffaaab'));
function sqrt3mod4<T>(Fp: IField<T>, n: T) {
  const p1div4 = (Fp.ORDER + _1n) / _4n;
  const root = Fp.pow(n, p1div4);
  assertIsSquare(Fp, root, n);
  return root;
}

function sqrt5mod8<T>(Fp: IField<T>, n: T) {
  const p5div8 = (Fp.ORDER - _5n) / _8n;
  const n2 = Fp.mul(n, _2n);
  const v = Fp.pow(n2, p5div8);
  const nv = Fp.mul(n, v);
  const i = Fp.mul(Fp.mul(nv, _2n), v);
  const root = Fp.mul(nv, Fp.sub(i, Fp.ONE));
  assertIsSquare(Fp, root, n);
  return root;
}

// Based on RFC9380, Kong algorithm
// prettier-ignore
function sqrt9mod16(P: bigint): <T>(Fp: IField<T>, n: T) => T {
  const Fp_ = Field(P);
  const tn = tonelliShanks(P);
  const c1 = tn(Fp_, Fp_.neg(Fp_.ONE));//  1. c1 = sqrt(-1) in F, i.e., (c1^2) == -1 in F
  const c2 = tn(Fp_, c1);              //  2. c2 = sqrt(c1) in F, i.e., (c2^2) == c1 in F
  const c3 = tn(Fp_, Fp_.neg(c1));     //  3. c3 = sqrt(-c1) in F, i.e., (c3^2) == -c1 in F
  const c4 = (P + _7n) / _16n;         //  4. c4 = (q + 7) / 16        # Integer arithmetic
  return <T>(Fp: IField<T>, n: T) => {
    let tv1 = Fp.pow(n, c4);           //  1. tv1 = x^c4
    let tv2 = Fp.mul(tv1, c1);         //  2. tv2 = c1 * tv1
    const tv3 = Fp.mul(tv1, c2);       //  3. tv3 = c2 * tv1
    const tv4 = Fp.mul(tv1, c3);       //  4. tv4 = c3 * tv1
    const e1 = Fp.eql(Fp.sqr(tv2), n); //  5.  e1 = (tv2^2) == x
    const e2 = Fp.eql(Fp.sqr(tv3), n); //  6.  e2 = (tv3^2) == x
    tv1 = Fp.cmov(tv1, tv2, e1);       //  7. tv1 = CMOV(tv1, tv2, e1)  # Select tv2 if (tv2^2) == x
    tv2 = Fp.cmov(tv4, tv3, e2);       //  8. tv2 = CMOV(tv4, tv3, e2)  # Select tv3 if (tv3^2) == x
    const e3 = Fp.eql(Fp.sqr(tv2), n); //  9.  e3 = (tv2^2) == x
    const root = Fp.cmov(tv1, tv2, e3);// 10.  z = CMOV(tv1, tv2, e3)   # Select sqrt from tv1 & tv2
    assertIsSquare(Fp, root, n);
    return root;
  };
}

/**

 * 1. https://eprint.iacr.org/2012/685.pdf (page 12)

 * @returns function that takes field Fp (created from P) and number n
 */

  }

  while (FpLegendre(_Fp, Z) === 1) {

---

**A confidential receivables facility on the XRP Ledger.** A bank opens a facility. Suppliers enrol, draw down against invoices, and repay. Every position is an encrypted balance on a public ledger, and the facility retires in tranches. It has executed on Devnet, and the point of building it was to establish exactly what an outside observer sees while it happens.

**The answer: it hides the amount of a confidential *transfer*, and balances — and nothing else.** ⚠ **Converting in or out publishes the amount in plaintext, every time**; only a `Send` hides one, so the figure entering confidential form and every figure leaving it are public forever. Who paid whom, when, and how often are public forever; the issuer can decrypt every balance; and one asymmetry matters — a *freshly initialised* balance is publicly recognisable as zero while a *spent-down* one is not. That is the protocol, not a limitation of this build. [**Trust model**](#trust-model) sets it out in full, and it is the section to read before any other.

> ⚠ **Devnet only. No mainnet writes, at any phase, for any reason.**
> Nothing here is audited, production-ready, or safe to put value behind.

**What it exercises:** Multi-Purpose Tokens (XLS-33) and Confidential Transfers (XLS-96), together. ⚠ **Not Credentials (XLS-70) or Permissioned Domains (XLS-80)** — gating an issuance to credentialled accounts needs a `PermissionedDomainSet` and a credential per supplier, which is a separate milestone that has not been built. The issuance carries no `sfDomainID` and the facility says so when it runs.

**It has a second output.** Building carefully against a young specification surfaces things its authors would want to know. XLS-0096 was created on 2026-01-15 and was still a Draft when this project began on 2026-08-16. Upstream marked it `Final` on 2026-09-03, in PR #604, and last changed it on 2026-09-10, when it took in errata this project filed. Both dates were read on 2026-10-18 (E-1, E-316). ⚠ **This paragraph and the badge above called it a Draft until 2026-10-18.** Those accumulate in [`UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md`](UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md) and are filed under [`docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md`](docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md), held to a higher evidence bar than anything published here.

> **Reading the citations.** Claims here carry a row id from [`CLAIMS.md`](CLAIMS.md), the register that governs what this project may say. **`E-`** is established evidence, **`F-`** a finding about the protocol or its implementation, **`P-`** a standing prohibition — something this project may never claim — and **`B-`** an open blocker. `ADR-nnnn` is a decision record and `REVIEW-nnn` a review round, both under [`docs/decisions/`](docs/decisions/) and [`docs/reviews/`](docs/reviews/); bare issue numbers are issues on **this** repository. Where a sentence here disagrees with its register row, the row wins.

<details>
<summary><b>Terms used below, if you are new to XLS-96 or the XRPL</b> — click to expand</summary>

| term | what it means here |
|---|---|
| **MPT** | Multi-Purpose Token (XLS-33). `MPTokenIssuance` is the issuer's object defining one token; an `MPToken` is one holder's position in it. |
| **Confidential balance** | A holder's balance held as an ElGamal ciphertext on the public ledger rather than as a plaintext integer. Two of them per holder: a *spending* balance and an *inbox* that receives transfers. |
| **`sk_A`** | The holder's own ElGamal secret key — the `A` is for the account. It decrypts that holder's balance and is a required input to the proof for a `ConfidentialMPTSend`. |
| **Encrypted zero (`EncZero`)** | The *canonical* ciphertext of zero — fixed and recomputable by anyone from public inputs. ⚠ It is written on first-time initialisation, merge reset and clawback only. A balance spent down to zero is a randomised encryption of zero and is **not** recognisable, so `EncZero` identifies how a balance became zero, not whether it is. |
| **Convert / Send / ConvertBack** | `ConfidentialMPTConvert` moves plaintext into confidential form; `ConfidentialMPTSend` moves a hidden amount between holders; `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` moves it back out. **Convert and ConvertBack publish their amounts in plaintext**; only Send hides one. |
| **Bulletproof / compact sigma** | The proofs a confidential transaction carries. **The composition differs per transaction type.** `Send`: a 192-byte compact sigma plus a 754-byte aggregated Bulletproof. `ConvertBack`: a 128-byte sigma plus a 688-byte Bulletproof. `Convert`: a 64-byte Schnorr key-possession proof. `Clawback`: a 64-byte issuer-side compact sigma — ⚠ **same size as `Convert`'s, different construct, different party**. `MergeInbox`: **no proof**. The Bulletproof dominates wherever there is one. |
| **`tec` / `ter` codes** | XRPL transaction results. ⚠ **A `tec` is *applied to the ledger*** — it consumes a sequence number and its fields persist — which is why a failed confidential transaction still publishes its ciphertexts, and why `fail_hard` matters. |
| **`fail_hard`** | The JSON submission parameter asking the node to discard a failing transaction rather than apply it. `TapFailHard` is the corresponding internal apply flag in rippled. ⚠ **Internal documents in this repository call this `tapFailHard`, which is this project's shorthand and appears zero times in rippled** — see [`docs/VOCABULARY.md`](docs/VOCABULARY.md). |
| **Family seed / master seed** | The base-58 secret an XRPL account is derived from. This project also derives the holder's ElGamal key from it, which is what makes the seed a permanent decryption credential. |
| **Dedicated Account** | The facility's own holding account. ⚠ **Never call it a vault**: an XLS-65 `Vault` cannot convert to confidential form, and XLS-0096's own unrelated use of *"Confidential Vault"* for this account has already pointed one reading at the wrong conclusion. |
| **UDS** | Unix domain socket. A local IPC channel that no browser API can open, which is the whole reason the signer uses one. |
| **XLS-65 / XLS-66** | The ledger's single-asset vault standard and its lending protocol. Both come up because a confidential balance does not compose with either. |
| **Amendment** | An XRPL protocol feature that must be voted on and enabled per network. Whether one is live is a *reading*, never knowledge. |

</details>

### Evidence a stranger can check without cloning anything

Devnet is a public ledger, and these four were re-queried and confirmed validated on 2026-09-01. The `MPTAmount` column is the disclosure argument in one place.

⚠ **On 2026-10-18 the public Devnet endpoint no longer served them.** `tx` returned `txnNotFound` for all four, because `https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234/` now keeps only ledgers from 5,171,980 onward. Devnet was not reset: the facility's accounts still exist (E-319). A full-history node or an explorer may still have these transactions, and this project has not checked one.

| what | `MPTAmount`, as the ledger stores it | hash |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfidentialMPTSend` — built, proved and signed by `signer/` | **absent; the amount is encrypted** | `9170912934A842CE90494E66485ADC82739B2276ECD48E2900A1F62A164F9DB0` |
| `ConfidentialMPTConvert` — entering confidential form | **`30`, in plaintext** | `79F16C9A160E920F6D60BE3B1B8ACE50F85D2FA39D26C173378EA34B6558A59A` |
| `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` — one facility tranche | **`95`, in plaintext** | `34117EFEFE2EFE5446B5C3C66F8089C99298637D4E315B16780F82D77ABD7FB0` |
| `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` — the next tranche | **`191`, in plaintext** | `C34363951C527E357E248B8D78712BF1740B895CFCB09FC4BC62A62F00C209BC` |

⚠ **Read rows two to four before believing anything is hidden.** Only the Send conceals its amount. Every entry into and exit from confidential form publishes its own figure, so retiring a facility in tranches publishes **every tranche size** — which this project first got wrong in its own walkthrough, where it was called *"the aggregate change"* (F-24).

**Re-run the commands rather than quoting the table.** A restated count going stale is this project's most-repeated defect, and every instance was written by an author who had the previous one in front of them (E-141, E-199, E-201, E-203, E-222, E-223). ⚠ **This sentence used to carry the running total and it went stale within one session** — the number lives in the register, which is the only place it can be kept true. The same applies to this document's prose: its status block asserted that no implementation existed while the signer was already running (E-222, with E-204 the analogous stale-scope incident).
